chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
You may wonder, as do I, and as do people everywhere: how could this great scholar have gained access to such truth, when all of the earlier scholars and the great guides and imams failed to do so? I would reply to you: a person has nothing except what they strive for.

Indeed, people are differentiated through their actions.

This is true even for the Envoys (Messengers) and noble Prophets… and there will be a different level for everyone according to their deeds in this world.

Our own great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho was given awareness and understanding by Al’lah, and he was distinguished by his outstanding deeds and his great and humane sacrifices. Al’lah did not give him anything except that which he deserved.

God says,

“And We sent it down deservedly, and with righteousness it came down.” ﴿1﴾

chapters.title: The Faithful Mentor and the Lost Judge
chapters.html:
He never uttered a single word unless it was ethical and enlightening, which demonstrated his sharp insight, cogent mind and sound process of thought.

He was imbued with a deep-rooted, profound sense of humanity and a discerning sense for the truth.

These are but a few of the many sacrosanct qualities embedded within him because of his great love for the Almighty, the Origin of sanctity; and this is why his words were like sacred gems enhancing the spirits of those who sought all that is right and true. These words were received in accordance with the listener’s status, and touched whatever occupied his spirit so that he could find the reality which was evident within them. He spoke whenever necessary and always in a manner which was appropriate for the listeners’ spirits so as to bring them nothing but goodness and happiness, both here and in the Hereafter.

His piercing insight and knowledge gave the effective cure for illness garnered from his sublime wisdom so that disease might be eliminated and replaced with sound health and happiness. Thus, the advice of this faithful mentor always resulted in benefits and happiness for his listeners in this world and in the Afterlife.

Everyone who came into his presence recognised his peerless realism and piercing insight by God’s Light. His unparalleled recommendations ensured deliverance and success and, by contrast, those who disagreed with his advice were deprived of these benefits and blessings and ultimately regretted their decision.

This was the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

The following event reveals an example of his Godly advice:

A certain hapless judge stood wringing his hands together… saying, ‘Oh… if only I had listened to your advice, Abu Fathi.’ Then, he began to relate what had happened to him in the hearing of several men, repeating yet again, ‘If only I had followed your advice, Abu Fathi!’

So, what is the story of this judge? What was the advice which he ignored and then regretted doing so?

It was during the 1940s, when the salaries given to state employees far exceeded imagination, and those who were employed were extremely fortunate, whether they were employed in a low position or a high one: a gendarme or an officer, as all their salaries were considered to be enormous. Their income was not simply a consistent trickle, but could be described rather as a continuously streaming river. The lowliest official received a monthly salary from which, within a year, he could save enough money to buy a sizeable house and a car; in addition to which all members of the family would enjoy the high life.

At that time, when the luxurious life for people in general and public servants in particular had eased off somewhat, the Ministry of Justice declared that it needed to appoint judges in its official courts.

The judge of whom we write was an acquaintance of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (Abu Fathi), and was one of those applicants who held the certificate of law. The list of names of the persons to be appointed was issued after a while and his name was among them. Needless to say, he was extremely pleased when he became a prominent official, a judge who would earn a large salary which was many times greater than that of an ordinary employee.

He completed the formal assignment papers as fast as he could, and took up his position a few days later; when he received his first salary, he realised that it was quite considerable. He then calculated his monthly needs and found that the amount he needed came to no more than a tenth of that huge salary. Then, an idea struck him whereby he thought that he could draw nearer to the state authorities by presenting himself as an honest and upright human being; so he sought to appear concerned for the state’s public interest, a caretaker of its budget, and honest and righteous in his employment.

He talked to Mohammad Amin saying, ‘Oh, Abu Fathi! As you know I became a judge, receiving a monthly salary that is so large that I need only one-tenth of it to live in comfort. I wondered what I should do with the remaining nine-tenths, and then I had the good idea of returning it to the state treasury, as it is rightfully theirs. So, I decided to write a formal letter to the authorities in the prime minister’s office and ask them to lower my wage to just one-tenth of the current amount.’

The august scholar understood the judge’s reasoning, which was that he cared to show himself as the very soul of honesty and fairness in the eyes of those in authority, but he advised him, saying, ‘Don’t ever do that. They have willingly given you this salary, and it is your right, yet if you find it is in excess of your needs, donate it as charity to paupers and others who are in need.’

The judge replied, ‘But, as I have told you, Abu Fathi, my salary is so large, and I have no right to anything beyond my basic needs, so in fact it belongs to the state, as nine- tenths of my salary is above what I need and I shall return it to the treasury.’

At this point, the candid admonisher repeated his advice and caution to the judge, ‘As I have told you my brother, give the excess as a handout to the poor and needy. You know there are a lot of destitute families in dire need, so if you spend the surplus amount on them you will have eased their embarrassment and saved them from poverty, deprivation and misery by securing for them the essential necessities of life. Through that you will improve their condition and bring them happiness: thereby you will draw nearer to Al’lah because of your noble deed. So, all of their happiness and liberation from the ties of poverty and deprivation will reflect on your worldly life by giving you happiness, joy, and true closeness to Al’lah, the Almighty… and furthermore, you will gain Paradises of bliss in the Hereafter. Be sure, my brother, that all creatures are Al’lah’s servants, and the more one offers them benefits the closer they will be to Him. Al’lah has opened the gateway of Paradise before you, so do not refuse to enter it. Seek Al’lah’s Satisfaction and He will surely be pleased with you and make many people pleased with you too.’

The judge heard the scholar’s true utterance denoting his sublime logic. Those peerless words encompassed great goodness in this life and in the life to come. He thought for a while, then he realised he could not refute these words and the truth and love for humanity and for Al’lah’s Satisfaction that they denoted. Yet, he felt that they did not conform to his wish to present himself as an honest, upright and zealous man before the people… and certainly not before Al’lah, the Almighty. This was his personal, unbending point of view!

Therefore, he did not abide by these Godly gems and divine advice, thinking that his success in this world would not be realised unless he continued on his intended path, so, he decided to carry out his plan. At the earliest opportunity he sent a letter to the authorities in the prime minister’s office stating that he wished to reduce his monthly salary to one-tenth of what he was receiving. He stated, as he had previously said to Mohammad Amin, that it far exceeded his needs and one-tenth of the amount would be sufficient, therefore he felt that he had no right to retain the extra money. He explained that his conscience and deep sense of patriotism dictated that he should return it to the treasury since it rightfully belonged to the state and not to him.

This odd and unprecedented communication was received by the senior personnel in the prime minister’s office. Really, it was such a strange letter, the likes of which had never been seen before! So, those concerned held a meeting to discuss the matter, and after spending some time in discussion and deliberation they found the judge’s communication to be illogical and certainly open to doubt, thus giving rise to many questions about the judge’s abilities, the state of his mind, and the soundness of his reasoning.

Finally, they reached the following conclusions, ‘Truly, this judge is not of sound mind and lacks reasonable judgement, for anyone who refuses money rightfully offered to him is not at all fit to judge others. A judge’s position is so sensitive and strongly related to the citizens’ matters and interests, and consequently to the cases that come before him, that whoever occupies this position must be of sound judicious mind and unerring thought. Accordingly, the judge in question, about whom we held this meeting, is not suited to that position; he must, therefore, be discharged from this sensitive post.’

Thus, the man was instantly dismissed from his position, lost his employment and was left without income. His actions, that he had thought to be so worthy, had gone against him, whereas he had thought that his request would serve to strengthen him in his office and raise his standing in the eyes of the authorities. He believed that by his actions all people would hear of his fairness, honour, and rectitude and that he would become the model for integrity and patriotism.

But, on the contrary, the matter brought him a most unexpected and unpleasant result. When he was informed that he had been dismissed from his position and stripped of his employment, he remembered the great guide’s advice and words of caution against his planned action, and the aim of his intention which was directed at attracting people’s satisfaction not that of Al’lah. So, the authorities became perturbed at his request and he lost the great gains which Al’lah had prepared for him and toward which the eminent scholar, Mohammad Amin, had guided him.

Then it was that he remembered the warning and admonition, and sighing deeply he said, ‘If only I had taken your advice Abu Fathi!’

He was the loser and deeply regretted his decision, but it was too late!

chapters.title: The Devil Was Thwarted and Confessed, “I have No Power over You”
chapters.html:
One day, our noble scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho returned to his home filled with a feeling of great happiness, as his love for God provided him with all that he needed, and His Satisfaction with him was his only aim and desire. Without doubt, honour is attained by rectitude.

Usually, everything was orderly and satisfactory within his household, but that day it seemed that something strange was afoot!

As soon as he entered the house he heard strange sounds and was most surprised for he was accustomed to an air of tranquillity pervading his home. What had happened?! Everything had been fine when he left, but now he was taken aback by the sounds of grief-stricken voices. He could hear women crying as if something terrible had happened. But throughout his noble life, whenever he was taken aback, our great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho sought refuge in his Provider, the Almighty, Who relieved him and saved him from every single difficult problem.

As always, the spirit of Mohammad Amin Sheikho flowed towards the place of the event, and then continued towards the Holy Mosque. It travelled to al-Ka’ba, which is honoured throughout the world for its holiness and purity and is the holy place where God sent down lights upon His Envoy (cpth); ﴿2﴾

and these lights continue to come down because this is the location of the descent of the Godly Manifestations. Our eminent scholar put his full trust in Al’lah, without Whom there is no refuge or protection, and he commended the case to Him.

Within a few moments quietness prevailed once more in the house, and the recent fear and confusion were replaced with tranquillity: all signs of distress and suffering had disappeared… and moreover all of this happened within a single moment.

The scholar’s wife then came out of the women’s quarters and walked towards him, as she had sensed his arrival. She began to tell him about the events leading up to that point, relating the reason for the loud voices and what had happened before he arrived home. She said, ‘Some of the women of the neighbourhood came here, bringing an epileptic woman with them. She was having a seizure and thrashing around on the floor. Her limbs were in spasm, contracting and extending in a most unnatural way, and her whole body was making involuntary movements. Foam was frothing from her mouth and her eyes were bulging as though they were about to pop out of their sockets. She was struggling to breathe… it was as though she was being suffocated, or someone was trying to strangle her. Then she became very pale and the pall of death covered her face… she was struggling so hard in an attempt to escape from seemingly inevitable death. It was really a terrible sight.

‘Her state was very distressing. All of the women were sure that she was just moments away from death, and they all started shouting and crying and lamenting.

‘A few of her female relatives brought her here, hoping that God would heal her through your blessing. The people advised them to resort to you because they know about your uprightness and piety. Although they had previously taken her to many physicians, who prescribed different medicines and tranquillizers and analgesics for her, but these attempts to cure her had achieved nothing. The doctors failed to cure her because they do not have any effective medicine for such diseases. Every one of their medicines only provided temporary relief. But as soon as you entered the house, she became calm and recovered as if there had been nothing wrong.’

Mohammad Amin understood the case immediately.

He said to his wife, ‘Actually, she is possessed by evil spirits. This has been brought about by her wicked associate from djinn-kind who wants to destroy her and lead her to hellfire. But she has resorted to us, “and anyone who enters your home seeking protection from you, you should protect them.” However, this case is very easy to resolve, as Satan’s scheme is weak. The evil webs that he weaves are weak and ineffective as they have no material existence, even though he acts against those who are deserving.’

The great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho could hear the cursed devil that had entered into the woman speaking to him.

It said, ‘I will leave her and enter you.’

The scholar answered in a loud voice, ‘And I will break your head.’ Then, he began to recite the noble fortresses, al-Falaq (All that’s coming to Appearance), al-Nas (Oblivious Humankind, Oblivious DJinn-kind), and al-Ikhlas (Sincerity), as he began to direct his mind towards God and his heart fully towards the Holy Mosque. It was not long before that obnoxious devil left the woman and the house, defeated and subdued.

Due to the timely intervention of Mohammad Amin the afflicted woman regained her health and was able to return to her normal life, for all the pain and the effects of the attack had disappeared completely. As a result of her recovery, a feeling of joy and pleasure prevailed in the house, and incomparable signs of thanks and gratitude shone from the faces of those present. They all then left the house giving thanks and praising Almighty God and asking Him to give the august scholar great rewards.

Later on that night, Mohammad Amin was lying in his bed, trying to rest. As he lay there, neither fully asleep nor fully awake, he felt, suddenly, the alarming presence of a black spirit. He heard it saying, ‘No fault! No blemish! There’s no way I can enter into you! I have never met a man like you, who is such a hopeless case for me!’ The black spirit then uttered curses at the scholar’s religion and fled, for fear of being burned by God’s Light when the scholar sought refuge in Him.

And if you ask about the reason that the Almighty God allowed the devil to curse and swear at our religion, it is because He, the Almighty God, just wanted to show Mohammad Amin the profound enmity of the devil, his disbelief, and his humiliation and ultimate defeat.

chapters.title: The Session of Truthfulness and the Voice of Reality
chapters.html:
His assembly (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) was a session of truthfulness, and his tongue was the voice of reality.

The gatherings of the noble scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, were scented with the essence of paradises and refreshment; they were flooded with blessedness so that true life would descend upon the faithful hearts who seek to know their Provider, and these gatherings would make their hearts fragrant, clear and tinted with shades of brilliance and purity. They would be illuminated by God’s Lights and cultivated by the jewel of His Supreme Attributes so that they will be reclaimed and refined. The low deeds they had previously insisted on would be abolished, releasing them from the chains which had confined them and prevented them from soaring into the orbit of truth and reality where the luminosity, the light, the beauty and the majesty are to be found. Here too is where the hearts of the grand Prophets and Envoys (cptt) melt when they witness the Greatest Treasure and the Origin of goodness and generosity where the sacrosanct Grants of the Almighty God, Glory to Him, are manifested.

Because of his truthfulness in guiding Al’lah’s creatures and his aspirations to bring the optimum goodness upon them, the Almighty made him a doctor for the hearts. To this end He disclosed to him the conditions of everyone who had resorted to him, with the aim of curing them and leading them towards the truth, if that is what they truly sought. Therefore Al’lah’s Light reveals to him the truthful man and the liar and shows him both the ailment and the remedy. It discloses to him the cause that drove some disciples to distance themselves from the Almighty, and where the fault might be, and the direction in which the spirits of others may scatter or incline. By Al’lah’s Light, he knows the cause which gives rise to a slackening in seeking its aim and requirement if the spirit really sought to be acquainted with Almighty Al’lah.

Thus, this venerable guide Mohammad Amin Sheikho was a healer for their hearts: it is he who saved them from their alienation from Al’lah and then invited, guided and led them to Al’lah, to the levels of closeness to Him, and to sublime paradises. That’s why the Almighty ensured that his heart’s eye was always observing them, looking by His Light at all their conditions and knowing their inclinations and inward thoughts.

And why should this not be so? For he was their spiritual doctor assigned by Almighty Al’lah to guide and help them to attain and realise the truth.

Mohammad Amin was so gentle, so merciful: his kindness towards his murids and disciples was limitless. If he wanted to refine a fault in the manner of a certain disciple, or draw attention to a particular weak point in one of them which might prevent him from persistence in adopting the way leading towards his Provider, he would do so in a sensitive manner. In order to show the murid the method and the medicine which would release him of the weakness he found in his spirit, the eminent guide would refrain from speaking out openly and frankly to the disciple about what he found inside him or pointing out his faults openly. He would, however, relate stories and lessons in which he would refer to the ailment and its appropriate remedy. Hence, and without being aware of it, this murid would receive a description of his complaint or the mistake he had made, along with the suitable cure and the necessary medicine to rid himself of the malady and reject what was making him withdraw from Al’lah which caused him to degrade his position and debase him with Al’lah, and fellow humans.

All this occurs by Al’lah’s Light, when the diagnosis for spiritual disease and the prescribed remedy were given through Al’lah’s Manifestation by His Light for this true guide and merciful, humane doctor to know the condition of his murids, and the methods for effecting a rescue, cure, and success for each one of them.

Indeed, this true master really astounded all people who sincerely sought the truth through his incontrovertible luminous science and his superb diction in guiding and directing those who had resorted to him for guidance in loving God and drawing nearer to His Presence, Glory to Him.

He had amazed all people who aimed at sublimity and attaining the heavens. Why not, since the Almighty God spoke through the master’s tongue, enabling his lofty revelation to flow in abundance.

At this particular seminar and assembly of guidance, there were more than four hundred murids from various cities and villages. They were all leaving after the sanctified lesson during which their hearts were filled with great light and measureless gratitude and praise for God Who had sent this grand blessing. Indeed, everyone of them had profited by gaining solutions to all his problems or a diagnosis for his ailments and the weak points in his spirit. Moreover, the master would have given him the medicine and an unfailing cure which would never miss the target since it had issued from the Almighty Al’lah through the tongue of this eminent true guide. All of this diagnosis and cure came through his kind stories, gentle words and actual, realistic lessons and incidents within which he explained a particular point of weakness, its causes, and the ways man can rid himself of it.

One wonders just how many questions they were concealing in their hearts, yet by the end of the lesson all questions were answered and resolved; and so it was with all doubts and uncertainty which would be replaced with lofty Godly Wisdom and the luminous certainty of shining reality. In this manner, all questions and doubts would be resolved without anyone actually voicing a question or stating his problem publicly! Even if the questions had arisen only in a person’s mind, they would be answered with cogency, logic and firm evidence by the end of the lesson.

Then the disciples would leave the session, their hearts filled with light and love for Almighty Al’lah, since everyone of them would have achieved his own aim and been made aware of the right way in proportion to his personal closeness, and his level of aspiration and desire to be acquainted with his Provider.

One would also see that in their daily life the disciples were ordered and fully followed the law learnt from their eminent master: visiting the master would have its appointed terms; and pondering on the creation of the heavens and the earth also had its own specific times, just as there are appointed times for praying. In addition, to achieve the maximum benefit, attending his assembly must have its morals and controls; and so it was with the special visits for their venerable guide which must be regulated and have particular conditions: they began at 8 a.m. and ended at 11 a.m. As for the midday period which lasts until the call announcing the afternoon prayer, none of the disciples was to disturb him because this time is specified for rest. In summer, the lesson usually started after the afternoon prayer and lasted until 10 o’clock at night; while in winter this lesson and sacred recitation began after sunset and also lasted until 10 o’clock at night.

One night, unusually, the lesson was prolonged. The venerable master had given his disciples the opportunity to ask questions within this general lesson. So, the brothers began to put questions to him and he answered all their queries and that special lesson lasted until midnight. After that they had no need to ask him anything, for they were accustomed to having the answer presented as soon as the question occurred in their minds. Moreover, each of them understood the lesson according to his closeness to his Provider, his rank and his own efforts and personal humane sacrifices. So, Al’lah’s Speech was recited and so was the scholar’s revelation and explanation of the Holy Qur’an. It was the same assembly and speech for all the disciples but the level of understanding was different for each of them depending on his status. In this way, every disciple felt that the words were directed to him personally, solving his problems and showing the way to get rid of his faults which impeded his advance and approach towards his Provider. He would then leave the assembly having fully understood the solution of his own matters through the grand truth which was revealed by Al’lah and put into words through the tongue of this venerable master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

When the disciples gathered the next day to recall and discuss the lesson, exchange ideas, review the thoughts presented and the recited Godly explanations, you would find each of them had grasped it and explained it differently from the others. This was so because everyone had drunk from the spring of this true Godly guide in a different state from the others, and according to his own rank, level of truthfulness, and personal problems and ailments.

It was the same lesson and the same speech, yet it treated every murid and every heart, every status and rank. This proves that it had undoubtedly issued from the Almighty God and was aimed at the simple truth for each of them individually.

In fact, all the brothers in the circle of this eminent master had witnessed and realised this description and did, in fact, live in this state, which is why it had never occurred to any of them to oppose the thoughts or the perception of another of his brothers during their discussions of the lesson.

In confirmation of this, Professor Abdul-Kadir Yahya al-Dayrani, the disciple of the eminent scholar, says, ‘If you attend the lesson of this august guide, you need not ask or enquire at all, since Al’lah Almighty unveils to him everything by what He reveals to his heart and then passes through his tongue. Therefore, during his lesson (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) the Almighty speaks through his tongue so that each disciple will hear his own personal reply and be guided to enhance himself.’

Indeed, many incidents, examples and various indications had happened to each one, individually, in his assembly and to every murid of his circle, thus verifying that this solemn master obtained his science from the Almighty Who had shown him the states of everyone that had recourse to him and drank from his true guidance. So, by the foresight granted to him by the Almighty Al’lah he was a doctor, a director and a guide for them, as his insight observed them by day and by night.

Once, Mr. Abdul-Kadir (the disciple of the honourable guide) was entrusted by his mother to sell a house she had inherited from her father. He complied with her request immediately and within a few days he had sold it and received the sale money.

Since he knew that his mother did not need this money whereas he, himself, was in dire need, he returned to her bringing the money and began to speak about his situation, yet before he could finish his explanation she interrupted him saying,

‘Oh, my dear son! Take all the money from the sale of the house and use it as you like!’

Truly, the money came at just the right time to help him to straighten out his financial problems.

What a miracle!

In the evening of the same day, this honest disciple went as usual to the lesson of his august master, and as soon as he entered the meeting room, and before he managed to take the hand of his venerable guide to greet him, a gentle smile appeared on the features of the master, who said, ‘Surely, no one loves you as your mother does.’

In another one of these incidents, this murid had eaten his lunch; he then took off his formal clothes and, being exhausted he soon fell asleep and slept for two hours, more or less. When he woke up, however, he found himself in some discomfort, and even more tired than before he took a nap.

As soon as the disciple entered the session that same day the honourable scholar, Mohammad Amin, approached those present saying, ‘It has been proved medically that it’s unhealthy to eat before sleeping.’ Surely, this was no mere coincidence!

Similar incidents and other, greater examples happened repeatedly with one or other of the murids of this truthful, august guide; therefore they asked him about nothing since they knew about his familiarity by Al’lah’s Light and his knowledge by Al’lah’s Informing and Witnessing of their states and all of their troubles. This is how he was able to explain matters to them and answer the questions which occurred in their minds. Thus, the tongue of this guide who directs people to the truth speaks only the simple truth, and his words come from the Almighty Al’lah. God says in the Holy Qur’an, “He does not speak out of his own inclination.” ﴿3﴾

Once, a consul of a certain Arab embassy visited the venerable scholar (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) to listen to his great Godly Speech. When the consul entered, the venerable master received him with his cheerful countenance which was alive with joy and vivacity, saying, ‘Welcome, Your Excellency, Mr. Ambassador!’

The consul replied, ‘Alas! How could I reach such a prestigious position… ambassador…! I’m only a consul, sir!’

The honourable master replied, ‘We’ve said it, accept it then, Excellency.’

The consul said, ‘I wish… that God responds to your statement!’

During the session, there was a wonderful, sublime and heavenly speech which so overwhelmed the consul with bliss that he did not want to leave. In fact, he would have liked to stay for a long time in this state of heart irrigation by the companionship of this venerable, true guide; but, unfortunately, it was out of his control as he had many commitments and another appointment relating to his position. So, when his visit came to an end he took leave of Mohammad Amin who bade him farewell and said that he hoped for further meetings with him. The consul then left in a happy and grateful state of mind.

When he arrived at his office a great surprise was waiting for him for he heard news which had such a great effect on him that he couldn’t contain himself for joy, and he headed back to the venerable master just half an hour after taking his leave of him. Then he arrived for the second time and knocked at the door; as soon as he entered, he happily approached the honourable master saying, ‘By God… by God, sir, you welcomed me and said, “Welcome, Your Excellency, Mr. Ambassador!” ‘

‘I have come to tell you that at the very moment the decision was issued to assign me as the ambassador for my country here in Syria, and the embassy and appropriate authorities were advised, you addressed me as “Ambassador”. The previous ambassador had been discharged and they didn’t find a substitute, so they have appointed me. Yes! When you addressed me as an ambassador the decision had already been confirmed and announced!’ How strange the matter of this venerable man is!

How great is the truth that comes from his tongue! Really, it’s the tongue of truthfulness! What can his rank and position be with the Almighty Al’lah, Glory to Him? The august master endorsed the ambassador’s new position and congratulated him wholeheartedly, saying, ‘Praise God for this favour my brother, and keep offering charitable deeds.’

chapters.title: A Terrible Accident Is Avoided by Giving Alms
chapters.html:
Come, travel with us dear reader, to experience something which you may have never thought about. Our journey will take us by road to Lebanon in the company of our esteemed guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and we shall see evidence of his great wisdom and discipline.

One day, our illustrious scholar decided to travel to Lebanon on business matters. He took his son with him, and some of his followers accompanied him too.

At the taxi station, he was not to forget what he and his brethren – who were travelling under his wing – should do, so he reminded them saying, ‘By the way, my friends! Have you paid alms before travelling?’

And as he expected, they had forgotten all about it; meanwhile he put his hand into his pocket and took out one Syrian pound to pay alms for himself and his son, in addition to which, he took half a pound from each of his travelling companions and gave it as alms to a poor man at the taxi station.

All of them gave the alms willingly and eagerly except one who was reluctant to comply, and dithered in paying it, even though he was rich and from a famous family.

Thereupon, the venerable scholar, Mohammad Amin, stretched out his hand quickly and grabbed the money from the hand of his hesitant disciple and gave it to the poor man; then they all got into the car which set off from Damascus, the capital of Syria, to go to Lebanon.

On the way, all was quiet inside the car… except the gentle, pleasant words spoken by the great scholar, Mohammad Amin, including his thoughts on mercy, relief and happiness for their hearts, through which he guided his disciples who listened to him with the utmost respect and courtesy; all the while his little son sat contentedly near the window looking at the charming views of nature unfurling as the car passed through the countryside.

The car was moving at an average speed when suddenly something happened quite unexpectedly: a big lorry was approaching it at the crossroads and it seemed that an accident was inevitable. The driver desperately tried to avoid the lorry by decelerating and turning hard right, but there was no time to avert an accident… for the lorry collided heavily with the taxi on its left side.

Walid, son of Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was sitting in the back of the car on the left side, still absorbed in watching the passing scenery, and when the collision occurred, the boy flew into the air as if a hand had carried him from the left and dropped him – thank God – in his father’s lap on the right.

Fortunately, none of the brethren were harmed either, except the laggard disciple who paid the alms only when he was shamed into doing so.

And so, it was that Al’lah willed that he should know the value of almsgiving before travelling and why the noble Envoy recommended it to us with an effective practical lesson; for the man that was reluctant to pay was affected by a slight injury to his leg that confined him to his bed for a full month.

The noble Envoy (cpth) spoke truly when he said, “Hurry to pay the alms for almsgiving will ward off affliction.”

chapters.title: He Cannot Be Blamed for Telling the Truth
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an the Almighty Al’lah says, “As He has already revealed to you in the Book, if you hear people denying and ridiculing God’s Revelation, do not sit with them.” ﴿4﴾

This is a Command of Al’lah, and whoever believes in Him should obey His Commands. No doubt, the true believer will show his good nature, forgiveness and tolerance when somebody behaves badly towards him personally, but if a man’s misconduct is directed towards God or His Envoy (cpth), he will become like a raging fury. For that man, there is no space for leniency nor gentle persuasion, when confronted with untruths or deception; rather, he will spring forth as a lion in order to uphold the truth, giving no thought to the price he might pay for his defensive reaction.

Every believer sets an example of personal devotion and self denial for the sake of God’s Envoy; he may sacrifice his wealth, dispense with friends and even offer up his soul when he senses any criticism of God and His Envoy. This is a distinguishing characteristic found in all people of true belief, while it is totally lacking in all hypocrites. Believing that their requirements and the arrangements of their affairs are controlled by human beings, those who have not fully understood the statement that “there is no god except Al’lah” frequently fawn over and flatter people of authority so that their worldly advantages and inferior desires may be easily fulfilled, unconcerned at losing all respect, and their demeanour being marked with obsequiousness and false humility.

Pitiful people!

They are unaware of the great remorse and pain they will inevitably suffer when the veil is removed from their heart’s eye at the time of their death, and this carnal and temporal world vanishes forever more. Only then will they come face to face with the reason for their existence and understand the sublime purpose lying behind it, and only then will they sense once again the nature of perfection which God had stamped upon their spirits. But at that time, it will be too late for them to repent and make amends for their wrongful conduct.

Out of his love for God’s servants and to avoid them experiencing such a sorrowful end, the august guide, Mohammad Amin, repeatedly admonished his followers to adopt the path that leads us to be proud of God and His Envoy and to avoid the path that may taint our hearts with lowliness and degradation. Relying on the noble verses of God’s Holy Book, he revealed to us how we should act if we ever met people who mocked God and His Envoy. His guidance was not restricted merely to his spoken words, but rather his behaviour was a practical example in support of all his teaching.

The following tells of a true incident that the noble guide experienced personally, through which he (God sanctified his secret) introduced a proof of his true and actualised guidance, and his magnificent zeal for the Grand God and His great Envoy was clearly expressed.

It is well-known by everybody all over the world that the Jews have set a clear example of loving this worldly life and wasting all the powers that a man may have in order to enjoy its abundant pleasures and vanities, instead of using their endowed faculties to recognise God and approach Him, the Almighty. And because of their insistence on expending great efforts to attain carnal enjoyments, God fulfilled their desires and placed the majority of the national wealth in their hands, thus making them the richest nation in the world.

During the lifetime of our noble guide it happened that a wealthy Jewish man, a famous merchant, came to visit some of the merchants and notables whom he knew personally, in Damascus. The men of Damascus received their visitor warmly, showing him great respect, and addressing him constantly with kind and gentle words! And how could they not express their great esteem for this man when his opulence was obviously so much greater than theirs! They competed with each other to arrange banquets in his honour; and how fortunate was the one who would have him as a guest at his home! This was their ill-considered view. As for His Excellency, the more the people around him humbled themselves and kowtowed to him, the more his insolence and presumptiousness grew. Sometimes he swaggered among them virtually submerged in his own pomposity and overwhelmed by his sense of pride and self-conceit, and at other times he sat nonchalantly with his legs crossed, turning up his nose at them whereby signs of contempt were clearly visible on his features.

At one particular banquet, he became increasingly full of his own self importance and began to scoff at his acquaintances amongst the Moslem notables and merchants, their religion and beliefs in particular. And yet, despite that all the present continued to smile politely, and failed to react to his loathsome behaviour. Not a man among them had a degree of faith and fervour for their Envoy (cpth) that would spur him to roar in his face and defend the truth, so that his cursed wrong would have been destroyed and his wicked devil along with it. What gives one cause to wonder, is that their position and behaviour towards him never faltered, on the contrary it remained as it was, coloured with boundless honour and glorification and ingratiation! But their reverence for the wealth that the Jewish merchant possessed reduced them to the lowest possible degree of contemptibility when he mentioned to them, mockingly, a noble saying of the great Envoy (cpth), and then he burst out laughing, and they laughed with him!!

‘Your Envoy said,’ the rich Jew began with a derisive sneer on his lips, ‘…that tomorrow the Jew will hide himself behind the tree, but then the tree will speak to the Moslems, “Come on, Moslems! There is a Jew hiding behind me… come on, kill him”.’ He laughed and again everyone with him, that is, those who could understand his language, laughed too!

It was God’s Will that our august scholar was invited to that banquet. When he saw a large group of the guests there laughing he asked some of them, ‘What does this Jew say that makes him and you laugh so heartily?’ And they told him the reason for their laughter. He was shocked, but more than that, there was a feeling of deep sorrow that penetrated into his pure heart for the state of those sycophants around that accursed Jew. There and then, a whirlwind of unmeasured compassion was brought forth inside his free spirit that made him burst out with unique, glorious, moral power in the face of that evil man. He shouted at him in a thunderous voice, ‘You, Khawaja!’ ﴿5﴾

The Jew, who did not speak Arabic, turned towards the source of the thunderous voice to see an awe-inspiring human being with an unparalleled mien that caused him to stand staring at him, his mouth agape and limbs quivering. ‘Listen… Khawaja’, the revered master continued while his hands gesticulated in an attempt to make the Jew fully understand the meaning of what he was saying. ‘Tomorrow… the Moslem (pointing to himself)… the Jew (pointing to the Jewish merchant)… a knife (with his hands signifying that he would hold a knife)… will slay him (passing the same hand over his own neck and giving a sound like that of a knife cutting through a neck).’ The meaning was perfectly clear and was instantly imprinted on the mind of the malicious Jew. There and then, the justice that dwelt within the spirit of the pure master clashed with the injustice and wickedness within the evil spirit of the wealthy Jew and stamped it out completely.

Then the Jew perceived a rampant lion stamped on the face of the noble master that caused him to become completely dumbstruck, as an overwhelming feeling of awful terror crept into his depths making him quiver from head to toe, and convincing him he was about to breath his last.

Yet the imposing sight of the august master was also highly impressive for all of the guests at the banquet, for having heard his evil-crushing words, their hearts shook violently. But how strange! When they should have been pleased that there was still a true believer defending God and His Envoy with such peerless zealousness before that ill wisher, they were alarmed instead, and their spirits became aggravated! Their reaction denoted an obvious fact: these people were definitely on the wrong path, and clearly pleased to be there!

Worse still, they appeared to be displeased because of the august master’s reply to their friend, to the extent that a few days later some of them declared their annoyance by criticising Mohammad Amin, saying, ‘He shouldn’t have acted in that way with our friend, the Jew; his behaviour was embarrassing and his answer was sharp. Why didn’t he simply ignore the man’s words?’ They did not want the prestige of their pompous, defamatory friend to be touched; and as for the prestige of God’s Envoy, they did not care one iota if the Jew belittled it, and even took pleasure in doing so.

No wonder! For when the carnal world becomes the chief concern of men and hoarding money their main aim in this life, then one should find nothing strange in such a shameful position and reaction.

chapters.title: The Woman Money Lender
chapters.html:
The Almighty God says in His Holy Book, “Whoever looks with the Light of God, God will give them salvation and provide for them whence they do not reckon.” ﴿6﴾

And in one of His Holy Sayings, He (Glory to Him) declared, “Oh My obedient follower, be for Me as I want you to be, and then I will be for you as you want Me to be.”

This is a law and something that, in reality, happens continuously when a human being becomes connected with God’s Robe, meaning Prophet Mohammad (cpth); and abiding by His Statute they will be close to God. Thus whatever good they ask from Him, He will definitely respond to them and fulfil their requests.

The more one is submissive to God and conforms to His sublime Legislation, the more beloved to God they will become and the more God will respond to their call.

Our humane guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was extremely close to God, and because he took great care to apply His Orders and to serve His creatures many incidents occurred that showed the effectiveness of this Godly Law and gave proof of the scholar’s high standing with God.

One of these events took place at the beginning of winter when the noble guide was concerned that his new house would not be in a suitable state to receive his disciples during the coming rainy days.

He had bought the house during the summer. It was an Arab-style house in the al-Muhajireen area, including a vast courtyard where fresh air always circulated freely. A fountain was located in the middle of the courtyard, surrounded by many beds of green plants and colourful flowers and roses which spread their fragrant perfume to captivate the heart and heal the spirit: it presented a delightful picture when one observed their bright beauty which the Godly Hand had produced and formed in all its excellence.

Like all other Damascene houses, the house of the noble guide consisted of two floors: the ground floor which was inhabited during the summer season while the upper floor was used in the winter. Both floors of this new house contained many spacious, sunlit rooms providing perfect ambiance and comfort to all.

But what distinguished this house from others was that whoever went into it would feel as though they were entering a garden of Paradise. This is because of the serenity and comfort they would sense within; they might experience a state of deep pleasure, or even of bliss: the kind of feeling that could not be found in any other house.

And it was no wonder, for the Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.” Our noble guide had dedicated his house to weekly religious lectures, and this was in addition to the special gatherings where he used to meet with his close and loving disciples. This blessed house was indeed like a Ka’ba, a focal point, for all his murids and all those who honestly sought truth, rectitude and religion.

When this great master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, reached fifty years of age he turned fully to devoting himself in spirit and time to guiding people towards God: leading their spirits into His Presence under his distinguished direction and the superior knowledge God revealed to him. He helped them turn to God and His Envoy with love, through the great realities he unveiled to them concerning God’s Perfection and His Supreme Attributes, and the truthfulness and noble merits of His Envoy (cpth). By virtue of the scholar’s endeavours in creating this feeling of love for God in the hearts of his followers, their spirits were refined and became imbued with the mark of Godly Perfection.

Large groups of young men, whether educated or not, joined his circle (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) where they could acquire great intellectual and spiritual fruits from the superior lessons they received from their teacher, and enjoy happiness simply by talking about the Supreme Attributes of God, the Almighty. These lessons breathed life and beatitude into their hearts and therefore they were unable to dispense with them for they felt them necessary to their daily lives.

Days rolled by and turned into weeks and then months, and summer faded, then autumn spread its colourful cloak; that too ran its glorious course and gave place to winter which brought with it chilly weather, heavy rain and snow.

With the onset of winter the noble scholar, Mohammad Amin, began to ponder upon the state of his new house and how it would fare in the coming rainy days, for it was the only place available to receive his followers who would be coming to drink from the fount of his heavenly knowledge. When he bought the house, it was still not plastered and the courtyard was covered with dust for it had not yet been paved. At the time, this was not a problem for him and his followers for they were still experiencing the warm, dry days of summer.

But on this particular day, thick banks of grey clouds covered the sky and veiled the sun; winds loaded with cool moisture began to blow, causing the rain to fall lightly at first. But it quickly increased and the heavens sent it in abundance.

The rainfall lasted long enough to turn the open courtyard into a large, muddy pool. The noble master came out of his room and stood beside the pool observing this new problem and wondering what he could do about it. He thought to himself, ‘Winter is here and the heavens have overwhelmed the earth with its blessings and rainwater; so, what can I do about this unpaved courtyard? I see that it will cause me some problems. Had it been only for me and my family it would not matter. But this situation will affect my disciples and the visitors who come here to learn about God!’

In fact, the problem might well affect more than three hundred people who were used to attending the lessons in person; and this number is apart from the groups who would visit him all during the week, morning and evening, to quench their thirst from his heavenly sciences. Unfortunately, the noble master was facing this problem at the same time that he was passing through financial difficulty, and so he did not have the money to solve it. He knew that the problem could easily be rectified by paving the courtyard, but this would cost a lot of money as the area in question was large, and he would have to buy the floor tiles and the materials needed for paving, also pay the delivery costs and the wages of the workers.

He had always been in the habit of keeping a sum of money to provide all the daily needs for himself and his family, and other necessities, including the alms he gave to the deserving needy. So whatever difficult circumstances he passed through, he carried all the burdens he faced easily and without any trouble, but with this new situation he felt a heavy load on his shoulders. He had to pave the courtyard as soon as possible because winter had arrived, but at the same time, he did not have the money to pay for it. So, what could he do?

He thought that he might borrow the necessary amount from his close disciples, but he realised that they were all poor and thus unable to cover the cost of the work. A feeling of anxiety began to flow into his pure heart when suddenly he heard a knock at the outer door of his house. The great guide walked steadily towards the door and opened it, and to his surprise he found an old woman standing before him although it was still early morning; the woman seemed to be strong and active even though she was advanced in years. He recognised her, for she was a famous usurer known not only to all the people in the region where she lived and, incidentally, where Officer Sheikho had once been the director of security, but many of the people of Damascus had also heard of her. She was well known for her abundant fortune, and her wide area of influence. In short, she was like a moving bank, for what she was worth was equal to, or perhaps more than, all the deposits in any bank. And now, this money lender was standing at his door holding a heavy bag. In a trembling voice she greeted the noble guide, saying, ‘Good morning, Abu Fathi.’

‘Good morning!’

‘May I come in, please?’

‘Yes, of course! Welcome, come in!’

She passed across the doorstep, still carrying the heavy bag, and then the noble master closed the door behind her. Once inside the house she put the bag down on the floor and revealed her careworn face, dripping with sweat. In a breathless voice she addressed the noble guide and began to tell her story, ‘Oh Abu Fathi! Last night I could not sleep at all. I was so afraid that burglars would burst into my home… at any moment I expected them to come over the wall… from all directions. Oh, sir! I was sure that they would steal my money and deprive me of so much of the fruit of my life’s work. I couldn’t close my eyes for even a moment. I waited, on tenterhooks, for the coming of morning, but it was needless for last night passed peacefully, but who knows what may happen tonight or any other night? So, I’ve decided to resort to your protection, sir. I can put my trust only in you, sir, for I believe in your honesty and truthfulness. I still remember your reliability and noble manners when you were the director of our region. I still remember your honourable conduct, therefore I find no-one to be more trustworthy than you, sir.

‘That is why I have brought these golden pieces for you to take care of on my behalf; in this way I will protect myself and my beloved money from the eyes of thieves and burglars. And with this I give you a full and free hand to take whatever sum of money you need and to spend any of it in whichever way you see fit. But this will be on one condition only, and that is to hand the full amount of golden liras back to me on the day I return to collect them. If you agree on this condition you can take the amount you need and I will not charge you any interest on it at all. I just want to find the full amount of money when I come back to get it. Here is the bag of gold coins, take it and protect it. Now I can go about my business with a peaceful mind. But again I remind you, when I visit you again I want to see it as I left it, with not a single penny missing. Do you agree?’

The noble master took the bag from the woman, saying, ‘As you like, but don’t you want a receipt for this money?’

‘Not at all,’ the woman answered, ‘a man like you who is entrusted with men’s souls can surely be entrusted with even the greatest amount of gold. No… No I will not take a receipt from you.’

However, the noble guide refused to keep the money in his charge without giving her a receipt which he wrote and signed with his own pen. And so, the woman said goodbye to the honourable master and left the house with a calm mind and tranquil heart. Her heavy steps expressed the exhaustion she suffered because of the previous sleepless night she had spent, worrying that thieves might break into her house and steal her bag of gold.

Glory to Him! How Great He is! He directed this woman to his obedient servant at the proper time, and did so even before Mohammad Amin prayed to Him to ask for His Help! It was only because the feeling of a heavy burden had begun to creep into his noble spirit as he thought of the new situation of his house in winter and joined it to his straitened circumstance, that the Almighty soon dispelled his worries by totally unexpected means. He sent to him a “moving bank” and placed at his disposal a sum of money, interest free, and many times greater than the sum he needed. Thus, the noble master was relieved of his worry and his features relaxed as he decided to borrow some of the woman’s money since she had willingly offered it to him. In this way, he could pave the courtyard and make some necessary improvements in the house so that the entire problem would be quickly resolved.

When the work was finished, the noble master was extremely happy for everything had been easily accomplished. He turned to God in praise for His Arrangement and Help which enabled him to continue his lofty lessons of guiding people to Him without any trouble.

Many days passed before another favour came from God to this noble guide when one of the shops which he had inherited from his late father was sold; so he took a part of the price he received for the shop, equal to the sum he had borrowed from the money of the money lender, and put it back in her bag after he changed it to golden coins.

That same evening our noble man went to bed with his heart full of immeasurable gratitude for the Almighty Al’lah (Glory to Him) Who supported him and eased the difficulties in his way, helped him to finish the work and return the money he had borrowed to the bag before the woman came back and asked for what was hers.

That night he closed his eyes, delighted and at ease, and surrendered to sleep. Then, as dawn broke the muezzin called for the dawn prayer, and so our great guide performed the communication with God and then he began to glorify the Almighty Al’lah. Suddenly he heard the echo of a voice as though coming from a distance. It reverberated around the entire quarter repeating one phrase, ‘I have missed it… I have missed it.’

‘How odd! Who could it be?’ the noble master thought to himself, ‘It’s still early morning, so who is shouting like this and in this area? Oh, God of all! I hope it’s good news.’

The quarter where he lived was known as the area where the upper class of society and the ruling element in Damascus lived and where silence and tranquillity constantly prevailed.

‘So,’ he thought, ‘who is causing this clamour and speaking in such a strange voice?’ But the answer was soon revealed when he heard loud banging on his street door followed by the same voice echoing the same words, ‘I have missed it… I have missed it.’

With this, he could guess who the source of all this noise was, so he got to his feet and quickly rushed to open the door. It was she, the money lender! She had come back to reclaim her bag of money.

Without any word of greeting she said to the noble man, in her Bedouin accent, ‘I’ve missed it… my money… my gold… I want my bag of golden liras.’

‘Okay… okay… you will have it,’ the noble master replied, ‘the gold is complete, not one lira less.’ She went into the house and the noble master entered one of the rooms and then came back holding the weighty bag and handed it to the woman.

She drank the delicious cup of coffee that had been offered to her and then said goodbye to the noble guide and left the house holding her beloved bag, not just with her hands, but seemingly with her eyes and heart too.

Behold, dear reader, the Wise Actions of the Almighty and Merciful God! Unaware of God’s Will and against her own will, the Almighty directed this money lender to relieve His beloved obedient servant of his distress and to alleviate his difficult circumstances. He sowed in her heart a feeling of alarm about the security of her gold and so pushed her to seek refuge in the noble guide and bring him, unconsciously, a release from his own anticipated troubles. He did not allow his obedient follower, the man of high intentions, to suffer straitened circumstances or to be put in any kind of tight situation.

Rather, He sent that woman at the appropriate time to solve his problem and, again at exactly the right time, He sent her back to reclaim her money after the borrowed sum had been replaced, and not a moment sooner.

If this demonstrates anything at all, it shows the great rank of this truthful guide with his Provider.

The Almighty says in His Holy Book, the Qur’an, “Every difficulty is followed with ease” ﴿7﴾

In this noble verse, Al’lah, Glory to Him, states a firm rule and effective law, “Whoever is straight in observing His Commands and Statute, He will assuredly raise his prestige and remove any difficulty that may stand in his way.”

This is true for every righteous human being. As for those whose difficulty arises in their spirits out of their care for the advantage of their brothers and sisters in humanity and for fear for their future in the Afterworld, and not out of any personal purpose, how high their spirits are and how close to God they are!

Let all humanity strive in that same way.

chapters.title: Success
chapters.html:
By Al’lah’s Wisdom, he who comes to our gathering will succeed, and he who does not will fail.’ These words fell on the ears of all those present at the assembly, so thereafter they paid even greater attention to what was being said. Indeed, it was a strange and wondrous prophecy! A prophecy to which their hearts submitted and which moved their deepest emotions. Oh, Provider! Is this true?

The meaning of that prophecy and its fulfilment assumed great importance after it had been explained by that august master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. So, what might it foretell? And why did it seem so astonishing? In fact, it was not a story but a real prophecy confirmed by Al’lah the Almighty.

We shall speak of two friends, colleagues at university, who were like brothers in their search for religion and the truth. Their characters were similar and through their close adherence to the virtuous eminent scholar they became just like two truly loving and sacrificing brothers, exemplifying brotherhood in its full sense. The men of whom we speak were Rateb and Adel.

They frequently attended the instruction sessions of their great guide… and always left together… discussing and debating… exchanging sincere advice, fully understanding one another’s point of view. They even went on excursions together, always in each other’s company, just as they were in the university, attending lectures and lessons together as they were both students in the faculty of Arabic language at Damascus University.

On that day something really strange occurred as Rateb attended the assembly of his guide without his great friend Adel, which all those present found most unusual, as did the eminent master who was prompted to ask ‘Rateb… my son! Where is Adel?’

‘Oh, sir! He has an exam at the university tomorrow, so he couldn’t come because he needs to study!’ Rateb replied.

‘What about you, Rateb?’ asked the eminent scholar, ‘don’t you have an exam too?’

Whereupon Rateb, with an air of prudency etched clearly on his features, said nothing… he did not answer his guide’s question. Then the venerable master stated, ‘By Al’lah’s Wisdom, he who comes to us shall succeed, but he who does not, will fail!’

These words made a great impression on all those present… the scholar’s words were truly astonishing… but more than that… it was a sensational and unexpected prophecy… all the more astonishing because Adel was the epitome of an energetic, hardworking student and the idea that he might flunk his exams was difficult to imagine. All those present were well aware that Adel was the top student.

He was extremely interested in his studies, dedicating ample time to fully understanding each of his quarterly subjects; he used to read every text book carefully and with great concentration. He never skipped a single chapter or lesson, or even the smallest detail without assimilating it fully; leaving no chance for unexpected circumstances which might occur.

Because of his dedication to his studies he became widely known to everyone for his diligence and academic success.

As for Rateb who was not so interested, nor showed such serious devotion to his studies, it would not be considered odd if he should flunk his exams, whereas it seemed to be impossible for Adel to fail, and for him to do so would be extremely surprising

A short time later the results were announced and the truth of the strange, astonishing prediction by the great master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, became apparent when the final results of the exam showed Rateb’s success and Adel’s failure.

That was a clear vision of the future, including firm guidance for the hearts of the attendees, all other disciples and, indeed, all people who seek the truth and religion. Thus it was demonstrated that an assembly of this imposing master should not be set aside in favour of other worldly matters as its duration is sacrosanct and contains guidance, healing and forgiveness of all sins and wrongdoing. At his gatherings the truth will be manifested upon the heart of the true believer, since we have come to this lower life for no other reason than to attain this truth and heart’s cure, while Al’lah Almighty ensures this lower life for us, so let us make it the means to an end and not the ultimate aim.

Indeed, let the sole aim be to achieve Al’lah’s Satisfaction which will be realised through attending the assembly of sacred Godly Science, because this lower world has been designed and effected for our advantage if we really seek to gain our Provider’s Satisfaction. The Prophet (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.”

chapters.title: The Compassionate Man and the Little Girl
chapters.html:
A hint of his great humanity and mercifulness

The position of guidance is of such great importance for it is based on the specific appointment of Al’lah and His Messenger, and not on mere memorised sayings and lessons recited from a platform. It is far more complex and involves leading by illumination, consciousness and witnessing, affecting and attracting the hearts of those whom one guides to the realities of the verses of the Wise Qur’an and to Al’lah’s Supreme Attributes.

This form of guidance is the most profitable as it acts in two ways: by the guide’s illuminated spirituality and his words, that is, he guides them as did Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth). By his own closeness to God he draws them nearer to Him and imparts to them qualities of perfection derived from Al’lah’s Supreme Attributes; and besides which he leads them by his knowledge which is founded on witnessing the truth and reality of God.

Such was the conduct of the great, esteemed Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah), the venerable guide who directs his disciples and followers towards the Sublime Presence of Al’lah by both his own spiritual state and great words. This kind of instruction and guidance to Al’lah is the most sublime, and it is through which he overwhelms everyone who turns of his own will towards him with a great desire of drawing near to God, so that they will have their characteristics changed and their spirits reclaimed, to be enraptured by, and bathing in the refreshing spring of Godly Perfection.

As an example of this, the disciple Abdul-Kadir al-Dayrani explained, ‘Within just one sitting with the eminent scholar all my personal traits have changed, as happened with the change of the spiritual characteristics of Pharoah’s enchanters ﴿8﴾

when they became illuminated by Al’lah’s Light through the company of our master Moses (pth), ﴿9﴾

and came to believe in Al’lah. I began to feel a flood of compassion in my heart for all creatures to the extent that once when I saw my little nephew, Hisham, playing with matches and lighting them, I gave him a little tap for I was afraid of the possible consequences if he were to repeat his dangerous game. Yet, in spite of that justified action my spirit blamed and censured me for hitting him, till I became immersed in a feeling of self-inflicted blame for what I had done, even though I had given that no thought whenever I disciplined or smacked the child before I met my dear guide. Therefore, I was happy to apologise to the child in such a way that he would understand the apology, and so that I might be released of the distressing effects of guilt and remorse. I knew that he liked to visit his grandfather’s house in Barzeh, a suburb of Damascus, so I decided to take him there. We went to the bus station, but we made a mistake and instead of getting on the bus going to Barzeh I took the one which goes to Erbeen. ﴿10﴾

At last, I turned back home with him and he was extremely pleased and happy, even though we had failed to visit his grandfather.

‘That evening, I went to visit my guide (the scholar) in his house, and no sooner had I seen him than I felt real light flowing into my spirit and a flood of mercy and compassion overwhelming my heart. Truly, through that grand master, the Almighty filled my heart with mercy and sympathy: he endowed it with the gem of Godly Perfection.

‘After that meeting, I never again hit any one of my nephews, and even so the reverence they held for me in their hearts so far excelled that which they held for their parents that the parents would threaten the boys that they would tell me if they were naughty. The mercifulness of this great guide for all creatures, which he derived from Al’lah the Almighty, was a pattern that one aspires to attain, along with the ceaseless guiding light shining from his heart, so everyone who turns with his heart towards him will have this guiding light flowing into his spirit which will be endowed with this same Supreme Compassion.

‘All during Mohammad Amin’s military service as an officer in the al-Sham gendarmerie cruel criminals and spiteful enemies tried to get rid of him by shooting at him using live bullets while he, on the other hand, faced them with the utmost mercy which flowed as calm oceans into his heart; so beside his real hand gun, he held a fake one with which he pretended to fire on them simply to frighten them. He was a man who hid his compassion and concealed his affection in order to show strength and firmness for his beloved child in a wise and beneficial manner.

‘In this way, he spent his entire military service without using a real hand gun against them even though he was holding it, so, when he eventually handed in the real one, the bullets were spoiled inside!’

The disciple Abdul-Kadir continued, asking, ‘Suppose a man has a cruel heart and lacks compassion… then, what could he possibly do to obtain it?’

As he had been disciplined by the great scholar, the reply was, ‘This kind of humanity should counteract his enticing spirit, so that he acts contrary to its own inclination, and does the opposite of what it requires him to do… for instance, if he found a dirty cat in his house and he was tempted to be cruel to the creature, he must counteract the temptation and never give in to it, so instead of rebuking or beating or getting rid of it, it would be better if he took immediate action to respect and feed the cat, and what’s more, if he could cleanse or wash it, he should do so. Let him remember and abide by the saying of Al’lah’s merciful Envoy (cpth), “Honour cats and she-cats.”

‘Furthermore, if someone talks badly about this man, and his spirit becomes inflamed with rage and he wants to pay his detractor back two-fold… here, he ought to quash his spirit’s evil whim and repay the offence with charity, such as giving a banquet and inviting him to honour and entertain him, and instead of invoking God against him, he should invoke God in his favour, wishing Him to cure his heart and rid the man of his malice and hatred, or his inhumanity. ‘So, if he adopts this great, illustrious path in contradiction of his spirit’s inclination, and opposes the call of the cursed devil, the Almighty will look into his truthfulness and change his imperfect character accordingly when His Light flows into his heart, wiping away evil from his spirit, and flooding it with His ever-flowing Mercy.

‘Thus, “Knowledge is obtained through learning, and Mercy is obtained by acting compassionately,” as Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) said. Besides, man should seek the company of faithful, true and merciful persons, because his spirit will be affected and acquire perfection through the company of perfect men amongst whom are those the Almighty made as guides to truth for ourselves, since they had been led by Him because of the great mercy folded in their hearts and which flows outwards to encompass the whole of mankind.’ Now, let us tell our story.

There was a knock at the door… and Ahmad entered.

‘Welcome Ahmad! Come in and sit down, my son.’ With extreme mercy, tenderness and cheerfulness, issuing from his merciful heart and which appeared on his noble countenance to revive and irrigate thirsty hearts, the venerable scholar welcomed his disciple who was still young at this time. It was the first day of Bairam. ﴿11﴾

‘What’s wrong Ahmad? You look sad… what happened? Tell me my son! Do you have a problem?’

At this, the good-hearted boy gave a long, tremulous sigh, and with innocent tears streaming from his eyes, he struggled to explain the situation, saying, ‘I don’t know… what can I say…? It was such a heart-breaking sight and it has upset me deeply. On the way to your house sir, I saw a funeral procession coming out of a house in al-Jisr al-Abyad (an area of Damascus). People were walking behind the coffin followed by a little girl crying and calling her dead father saying, ‘Oh Daddy! Who will give me the gift this festival?’ And then the mourners told her to go back home.’

Ahmad continued to describe what he had seen and heard which had painfully affected his heart, while the tears of the compassionate and venerable scholar began to fall from his gentle eyes, glistening like jewels on his pure cheeks, as abundant streams of Godly Mercy flowed from his pure heart to overwhelm all who were present.

A short time had passed when Mohammad Amin said, ‘Enough… my son! You have broken my heart… for God’s Sake, please… enough! Come on… hurry up and take me to the house from which you saw the funeral leaving.’

Immediately, the scholar with the great merciful heart stood up and, accompanied by Ahmad, walked quickly till they arrived at the house.

When the merciful master knocked at the door a little girl, about six years old, came out with her older brother… she was the daughter of the man who had passed away… the very same girl who had wept so desperately for her father.

The merciful master, Mohammad Amin, looked at her with eyes full of compassion and sympathy which overflowed to soothe the child’s grief… then he took a bag of money from his pocket, and gave it to her brother, saying, ‘My son, take this… give it to your little sister and tell her that her father sent this money as a festival gift for her.’

chapters.title: He who Listens Will Hear Good Advice
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an the Almighty says, “You who believe, do not push yourselves forward in the Presence of God and His Envoy but remain beneath Al’lah’s Light. Al’lah hears and knows all. You who believe, do not raise your voices above the Prophet’s, nor speak aloud when addressing him, as you do to one another, lest your good deeds be cancelled out without your perceiving it. It is those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Envoy whose hearts Al’lah has tested and proved to receive illumination by His Light.” ﴿12﴾

These noble verses clarify that anyone who truly believes in God does not put his own point of view before that of the greatest Envoy (cpth). It is impossible for them to do that since they have realised that his words (cpth) are the Words of Al’lah (Glory to Him). As for those who do not recognise his prestige (cpth) nor the prestige of any true guide who is a successor of the Envoy (cpth), they may consider their view on some matters to be more appropriate than that of these great human beings.

The Envoy (cpth) judges according to God’s Judgement; all his decisions are inspired by God and he refers to God in all matters. Therefore, whatever case may be laid before him, his judgement will be true and his words decisive even if he does not ask for full details of every point of the case.

In one review of his memoires, Professor Abdul Kadir John, alias al-Dayrani, a disciple of the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, acquainted us with an incident that took place during the lifetime of his truthful guide. He related the incident as follows:

‘My brother, Basheer, was a disciple of our great guide. He had a friend called Mahmood Abu-Sabha whose father had died. This young man was good-hearted and of a noble mind. Basheer convinced his friend of the great advantages to be gained by attending the lectures of our truthful guide, the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. And so, his friend joined the circle and began to attend the revered lessons, which caused my brother’s affection for him to deepen.

‘When our imposing scholar saw the newcomer at his lectures and sensed his good and noble merits he loved him and sympathised with him after he learnt of his poverty and that his father had died. A few days later, I saw our noble guide in a vision one night, saying to me, “Listen to me, Abdul Kadir, go to your brother Basheer and advise him to be a good friend to Mahmood. As for you, I want you to maintain your company and good relations with Abu Waddah.”

‘Abu Waddah was a friend of mine, endowed with the simplest and best heart of all my friends. And so, when I woke up I went to my brother’s house and told him about my dream. He listened to the advice and acted upon it, which made him draw ever closer to his poor, fatherless friend. And so was it with me. I behaved according to the directions of my teacher and maintained my firm friendship with my companion Abu Waddah. In fact, Abu Waddah and I had been friends since childhood and therefore we loved each other; but my love for him grew stronger when he began to attend the lectures of our imposing master and we became brothers in God.

‘Once, when I visited him in his house, as was our habit, his sisters passed before me unveiled. This was an abhorrent situation for me and one which I always avoid, for the socialising of males and females is a clear infringement of God’s Statutes. I had to tell him immediately how annoyed I was and said to him quite frankly, “Please, Abu Waddah, if you want our friendship and our brotherhood in God to last you must prevent your sisters from showing themselves to me.” He did indeed comply with my request; and after that I never caught sight of any of his female relatives whenever we spent time together in his home. Thus, our companionship and friendship became deep-rooted, and then when my venerable master advised me to take care of him it grew even firmer, and so it remained until he departed from this earthly life (may God have mercy upon him).

‘And now, let us return to our main story:

‘When the young man Mahmood Abu Sabha joined the national service, he went to one of the recruits’ assembly points; this particular one was situated in the al-Nabek area. A few days after his departure, my brother Basheer missed his friend and wanted to visit him in order to make sure that he was well and to see if he needed anything in this new stage of his life. And so, he decided to travel to al-Nabek to see his close friend. Mahmood Abu Shnaq, another friend of Basheer’s, and also a disciple of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, wished to accompany him on the visit.

‘And so, the two brothers in God met together at the agreed time and headed off to the house of our venerable guide to ask his permission for them to travel to the al-Nabek area to visit their young friend, Mahmood Abu Sabha. When Basheer arrived at the home of the venerable guide he was in his room, so he knocked as was the polite thing to do, and entered the room to ask for his master’s opinion about their planned journey and their reason for it. The revered guide looked at his disciple Basheer and then said to him, “Basheer, my son, do not go there.”
