‘“Yes sir, whatever you say.” Basheer replied and then took his leave.

‘In the large room which the eminent scholar assigned for his visitors, Mahmood stood waiting patiently for his friend, and when he saw him coming out he approached him asking, “Have you told our master about our intention to travel, my friend?”

‘“Yes, I have,” Basheer replied, “but he wants us to forget it; he said that we shouldn’t go there.” Mahmood remained silent for a while, turning over the reason that made their guide disagree with their travel plans and then he said to his friend, “Oh Basheer, I think that our tender-hearted master doesn’t want us to suffer the difficulties of this visit because of his compassion for us. You know, my friend, the weather in that area is extremely cold and today it’s snowing, so there will be little traffic; it will be very difficult to find transport going there or coming back. But, I think that you should go back to his room to explain to him that if his response is based on his fear that we may face difficulties on such snowy days, tell him that we will happily put up with anything in order to visit our brother Mahmood and be sure of his well being.” Basheer was convinced by his friend’s point of view so he returned to the room of their exalted guide and put their thoughts to him. With this, Mohammad Amin told him that they should do as they wished.

‘When Basheer told his friend about their master’s reply, Abu Shnaq said, “Didn’t I tell you, my friend, that our tender-hearted guide was reluctant to agree to our journey simply because of his great concern for us? Come on, let’s leave right now so that we can find a bus going through the al-Nabek area so we can leave early, and return early too.” There and then, the two friends hurried off to the bus station in Damascus where they boarded a bus and sat beside one another.

‘Two hours later they reached al-Nabek, wherupon they got down from the bus and stood on the main road which ran all the way from Damascus to Aleppo. They stood there for more than an hour, waiting for any car that might take them to the camp which was located about two to three kilometres away from the main road. By then it was snowing heavily; a bitter chill began to penetrate into their bones and still no car passed by. They thought that the road must be impassable to traffic, so there was nothing for it but to start out for the camp on foot, shuffling along the snow covered road. It took them one and a half hours to reach their destination after a long, hard struggle against the blinding snow storm.

‘At the main gates of the military camp they told the guards standing there that they wished to visit their friend, the soldier, Mahmood Abu Sabha, and asked if they would kindly call him… and then they stood aside, waiting. After half an hour that seemed like eternity as they waited in the harsh conditions, the guard returned and told them that the soldier they wanted to meet had been stood down due to health reasons and had left the camp heading to Damascus! Although the news was quite a shock for them, it was, nevertheless, a pleasant shock.

They were happy that their good-hearted friend had been exempted from national service.

‘All of a sudden, a feeling of astonishment came over them as they remembered how their inspired guide did not want them to undertake this journey, as if he had a premonition that the only outcome would be exhaustion and a difficult situation for both of them.

‘Again, bearing chill and snowfall, they retraced their steps on the snowy road back towards Damascus, passing the turnpike on their way. And it must be said that their way back was no easier than their way forward! It took one and a half hours of trudging back along the secondary road until they reached the main road which lead to Damascus. There they stayed for a considerable period of time in very difficult weather conditions hoping for the arrival of a bus coming from Homs or Aleppo and heading towards Damascus. At last, just as they were giving up all hope, a bus arrived and they began the return journey which lasted more than two long hours!

‘In fact, the entire journey caused them nothing but disappointment and suffering and brought them no benefits at all.

‘When they reached the city, they soon headed to the house of their noble guide where they found their friend Mahmood, the ex-recruit who, after mutual hearty greetings, began to relate the story of his dismissal which had occurred by virtue of Godly Providence. On their part the two adventurers told him the story of their exhausting journey which had taken the entire day, and the long hours they had spent exposed to the bitter cold and the driving snow. Indeed they were very sorry that they had not heeded the advice of their honest mentor. Had they listened to his words of advice, they would have spared themselves all that suffering and exhaustion: the only “fruits” they gained from that fruitless journey.’

chapters.title: The School Director Acts upon Wise Advice
chapters.html:
Here we shall tell of yet another honourable event that occurred during the noble life of Mohammad Amin Sheikho. It demonstrates his wise guidance based upon his prodigious superior knowledge of Al’lah, as it shows the positive benefits that Al’lah bestows upon him who follows his supreme guidance.

Without prior appointment Mohammad Amin Sheikho, the venerable guide, decided to visit one of his disciples at his place of work, so he hurried off with this in mind. The disciple held the post of a director of one of the top schools in the most elite area of Damascus.

On this particular day, while he was absorbed in his work and compiling some lists, there was a knock at the door.

‘Yes… come in…’ he called out. He was most surprised to see his revered master visiting him at his office! He stood up immediately to welcome him politely, and bent to kiss the master’s hand as he uttered warm words of welcome and happiness at the unexpected visit. Mohammad Amin returned the greeting with his usual kind words.

The great master sat down while his disciple, the director, asked permission to gather the files before him and to finalise some work in which he seemed to be engrossed, for then he wanted to be able to give his full attention to honouring his master. The great guide could not fail to notice that he was preoccupied with his paperwork, and asked him, ‘Oh son! What are you so busy with?’

‘Oh sir… it is my school,’ he replied. ‘The number of pupils has exceeded the maximum permitted, so the Ministry has ordered me to compile lists of the names of all the extra pupils whom I suggest to be transferred to another school which has vacancies.’

Mohammad Amin remained silent for a little while, then he addressed his disciple asking what he proposed to do about the situation.

The director answered, ‘Oh sir! I’m sitting here preparing these lists… but I have just stopped because of your welcome arrival. I’ve selected all the lazy and disorderly pupils and compiled lists of their names. I’ve decided to keep only the polite, hardworking ones in my school… sir.’

The wise guide hardly waited for his disciple to finish speaking, and, astonished at the course of action he was taking, interrupted him saying, ‘Praise is to God Who has sent me to you at precisely the right moment before you deliver those lists to the Minister.’ The school director was astonished at the words of his guide and he immediately began to wonder if he had done something wrong, or if he should have handled the matter differently!

The wise master, Mohammad Amin, continued, ‘Oh son! Don’t you want to do a good deed by which you will receive God’s Satisfaction? Don’t you want to keep for your life to come whatever may bring you closer to Al’lah? What effort are you making for the sake of God? What will you gain if you take the easy path and retain the hardworking, studious pupils? Those you want to keep at your school are naturally diligent, so it requires relatively little effort on your part to educate them, but as for those you suggest should be transferred, they are the ones who require you to strive and make great efforts to educate, and take care of. This single act will lead you to earn much for your life in the Hereafter, but if you move them to another school, you will be deprived of the deeds that Al’lah has directed towards you so that you may gain from this experience, and for your spiritual improvement. No son! This is the wrong course of action… you would do far better to transfer the diligent pupils and keep the lazy and troublesome ones.’

When told by the Ministry to reduce the number of pupils at his school, the director had seized this as a convenient opportunity to keep the hardworking pupils and send away all those who were lazy and disruptive, and by so doing he would attain superiority over all the other schools because of the high success rate of the excellent pupils in his school: something which would bring him great acclaim and praise from the Ministry of Education. But now, with the advice that he had received from his esteemed guide, he could not ignore this guidance and he chose to abide by this instruction as the merciful guide was greatly revered not only by his disciples, but also by everyone who had ever met or befriended him. Without fail all could sense the dignity and reverence held within his heart.

He answered, ‘As you wish, sir! I’ll do as you say.’

He immediately cancelled the first lists and prepared new ones containing the names of his exceptional pupils, and gave them to an employee with instructions to deliver them to the Ministry of Education on that very day. He did this even though it went against his personal inclination. The Ministry approved the lists and the pupils were removed to another school soon afterwards. It was not long until the administration of this school recognised the standard of the new pupils they had received and compared it with that of their original pupils, then they were extremely surprised… and somewhat confused!

It was clear that the lowest achieving pupil among them was of the same high standard as the previous superior pupils at the school and even surpassed them! Those pupils were supposed to be the lazy ones of the first school that we mentioned, so how can the pupils of the lowest standard compete with their excellent pupils? Therefore, they were full of admiration for the administration of the school where those pupils had been taught previously.

If the under achieving pupils of the first school are of such a high standard and so successful, then what about its top pupils? Truly, the school administration deserved great admiration and praise for its teaching plans and the tremendous efforts expended in preparing its pupils to achieve a standard that had never been attained by any other school: and all of that is by virtue of its director who is highly qualified to control all matters, and directs his school most ably towards such excellent achievements.

Of course, this was an erroneous train of thought, for they would never believe that the superior school had sent them its excellent pupils while they retained the lazy and troublesome ones. Now the director of the second school informed the Minister of Education, who happened to be his relative, of the excellent standard of the pupils sent from the first school.

Then the Minister wrote an official letter of thanks and praise for the excellent efforts of the director of the first school. The letter contained the greatest commendation for the highest standard of teaching in the country, and it was sent out to all schools with the directive that they should follow in the steps of this school which was the first in knowledge and development.

The disciple director was greatly surprised with the superb commendation for he had certainly never expected such a result; but he was wise enough to realise that he had attained this position by his compliance with his great guide who only wanted for him the rewards of the life to come. And so, because he had followed the enlightened teaching of his guide Mohammad Amin, Al’lah granted him the rewards of both this life and the Afterlife.

Similarly, Al’lah will be pleased with any man who seeks the Satisfaction of the Great Creator, and will make human beings satisfied with him too.

So, let man’s intentions be concerned solely with receiving God’s Satisfaction, seeking through his deeds the reward of the life to come rather than that of this temporary life. Let his only purpose be to please God, then he will attain happiness in the two abodes, and the men of truth should offer good deeds in the pursuit of such high aims.

chapters.title: The Curer of the Spirit Treats the Curer of the Body
chapters.html:
The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Communication with God is the route of ascension for believers.” The spirit that believes flows toward the venerated Ka’ba during its prayers whence it rises up to Al’lah, the Almighty, by means of the companionship of the noble spirit of God’s Envoy (cpth) which is always present in God’s Presence. This is the way that true communication is achieved with Him, the Almighty, and it rises ever higher in witnessing His Supreme Attributes. This is the reality of prayer which every true believer performs, as long as his belief is combined with strict adherence to God’s Commands.

As for those whose belief and faith are based on mere tradition and imitation, they may commit infringements and breaches of the Godly Statute, therefore their prayers will be imperfect and will produce for them nothing but sentiments and spiritual states which do not grow sufficiently to enable them to ascend to the High Presence of God and witness His Beauty, (Glory to Him). And sometimes it may even be restricted to mere words and gestures.

The faithful, eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (God has sanctified his soul) spared no effort in encouraging his followers to attain this level of communication with God, and urged them to reach this basic stage of true prayer whereby the spirit of a prayer would leave its body and travel to the holy Ka’ba where it would be able to communicate with God through the scholar’s companionship. For the scholar was their leader who guided them to God, the Almighty, and so whoever loved him and held a bond of reverence for him would soon enter God’s Presence during their true, heartfelt prayers, and soar up from the foundation of ascension which is the holy Ka’ba.

Scholar Sheikho invited people to worship God alone, and because of his distinguished teaching and logical and effective interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, the flower of the youth of our country, Syria, and of many other countries, joined his circle to drink from the spring of his heavenly sciences of realities and certainty.

Dr. Badr al-Din Atfah, husband of a granddaughter of the eminent scholar, was a young man distinguished by his good heart and admirable personal qualities. He never missed any of the lectures of truth given by our noble guide, which in reality were sessions of the great Envoy (cpth). For he (cpth) said, “Still I will manifest myself in the noblest man among you.” Indeed the scholar’s assemblies were like holy, heavenly Gardens during which all his students spent happy, sacred times whilst gaining sublime knowledge.

Dr. Atfah was one of the scholar’s murids, his committed followers, who reaped precious fruits from these inspiring lectures. The words of the eminent guide refined his nature and embraced him with his sanctified spirit until the doctor’s own spirit became totally clear and transparent, and adorned with Godly Lights. In this way he was able to attain a high level of true communication with God, just as this noble master wished all his murids to do.

But, unfortunately, this enviable situation did not last with Dr. Atfah; something happened to upset the serenity of his life and cause him great dismay. One day he came to his teacher to talk to him about his problem in words full of sorrow, ‘Oh sir, by God, I used to be able to flow spiritually to al-Ka’ba and perform true heart communication with God through your companion, but now I feel that my condition has changed and so my communication with God has ceased.’ Indeed, by virtue of his association with this truthful, august guide, the disciple, Dr. Atfah, had reached a high state of closeness to God and attained real communication with Him during his prayers. His spirit was able to soar to the Godly Presence after he bound himself to his imam’s spirit in the holy Ka’ba.

So, what was the matter with him that caused his condition to deteriorate so that he was no longer able to ascend to that lofty Presence to be in true communication with God? In fact, the underlying reason for this regression was his practice of the medical profession through which he was obliged to meet women, the young and not so young, to examine them, talk to them about their illness, and give them advice and prescribe medication. This caused his spirit to be distracted from its previous truthful direction towards his noble guide and weakened its link with the Provider, thus it had become once again confined to its physical body, unable to soar towards its Creator during prayer. The goodhearted doctor had lost his true communication with God which our virtuous master explained to him, and which the Envoy (cpth) spoke of in his noble sayings. His spirit had lost its clarity because of his communication with the gentle sex, for any source of evil which the eye catches reaches the heart and harms it. This is always true even if there is no evil intention. So, this was what now prevented the spirit of the faithful murid from reaching al-Ka’ba and praying there.

He had studied medicine, not out of his love for the profession, but simply to please his father who was a majorgeneral in the Syrian Army and a minister of defence at that time. The father had the highest aspirations that his son would follow a dignified career, so he forced his own will onto his son and ordered him to study medicine. And so, he fulfilled his father’s wishes, and as he had also entered the military college he graduated as an officer and as a physician. Dr. Atfah held in his heart a deep love for his guide, Scholar Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) so his strong attachment to him enabled the young man to attain true communication with God during his prayers. His spirit’s close association with the noble spirit of his mentor helped it to flow to the venerable Ka’ba: the base from which every truthful, obedient believer soars up to God, the Almighty. This is the positive fruit that every spirit reaps from keeping company with a true mentor.

The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Man adopts the faith of his close friend; you should therefore be careful when choosing an intimate friend.” ﴿13﴾

Yet when this doctor engaged in his profession and treated any woman, his elevated state went into decline, and sometimes it even vanished completely; and with this, his true communication with God was lost. The new condition of this murid did not go unnoticed by his guide, who became more watchful of him and asked God every day to forgive the sins of his follower. This invocation does not consist of mere words and prayers: rather it has a reality known only to those believers who are endowed with heart insight.

The noble mentor was directing his own spirit, which was wholly immersed in God’s Light, towards the spirit of his murid in order to overwhelm it with this same Light; thus every piece of filthy evil that had become ensconced in it because of his professional experience and his unwillingness to treat women would be eradicated, and thus his spirit would be cleansed and cured.

This was the course of action of this merciful guide with all of his followers; he kept his eye on them, embracing them with his lofty state, seeking God’s Pardon for their sins and helped them to draw close to Him by virtue of his own great closeness to Him. Like an eagle which enfolds its chicks under its wings, looks after them and protects them from danger, so was our revered master with his followers. He fought the devils which approached them and deflected them from his followers.

Now we shall return to the good doctor, the subject of our story, and the difficult situations he experienced.

Poor doctor! Whenever he left his clinic in the evening to go home, waves of severe pain and distress began to attack him, causing him to feel overcome with exhaustion. One evening, while he was on his way, he suffered severe pains in his head causing him to groan out loud,

‘Oh my head… Oh what’s this persistent headache? Oh my bones… I feel as if they’re broken… not just my bones… every atom of my body is causing me terrible pain… oh… I feel that I have lost all my strength.’

He was so exhausted that the moment he reached the house of our noble guide and entered the large hall he threw his huge, weakened body to the sofa. The noble guide was already fully aware of the debilitated state of his disciple, the physician. How could he not be so when his heart’s eye was constantly observing him and looking after him. For to be a true guide, first you must possess the insight illuminated by God’s Light that allows you to witness realities and attain certainty. Only then can you be of benefit to your disciples, for you will constantly follow them with the heart’s eye and with certainty, observing their condition and cleansing their spirits with the luminous Light of God.

A few minutes passed before the noble guide called for his exhausted, stressed murid, ‘Dr. Badr, my son, would you kindly give me an injection in the muscle? Come on, son, take this solution and inject it into my body.’ The good-natured doctor could hardly summon the strength to stand up on his feet, but with slow, heavy steps he walked towards his medical bag and brought out a clean, sterilised syringe. He took the solution from his master’s hand and drew it through the needle, then, having sterilised the tip, he inserted it into his guide’s noble body.

‘Good health, sir,’ the doctor said to his guide, with his customary politeness.

How wonderful! As soon as the doctor finished his work with the noble guide, his own condition changed completely; his weakness turned to strength, his suffering vanished and his usual levels of activity and vitality were instantly restored. An overwhelming feeling of happiness flew into his heart and a light spread throughout his limbs and body to crown his spirit so that it shone with renewed contentment and joy. How strange! What was the secret of this needle? For its effects were amazing, not on the tender-hearted master to whom it was administered, but rather on the doctor who had administered it! Indeed he seemed like a lion that had been freed from a severe, debilitating cramp.

A close follower of the eminent scholar was also present at that time and witnessed Dr. Atfah’s reaction after rendering this simple service to his guide. He noticed that the good doctor improved instantly to become bursting with vitality, his face glittering with radiance. The noble guide saw this follower looking with astonishment at Dr. Atfah so he said to him, ‘Oh my son, he cures my body and I cure his heart.’ ﴿14﴾

Oh God! Who was this noble man? What was his reality? His firmly established faith in God had produced a power that could, by God’s Leave, turn weakness into strength, and a feeling of complete exhaustion into renewed youthful vigour and determination! Indeed, Scholar Sheikho offered everything he possessed in order to save humanity from darkness, by following in the steps of his role model, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth), who had declared in one of his noble sayings, “I have sacrificed my body and soul for the sake of my whole nation.”

Driven by this lofty intention, he decided to have a daily injection at the hands of his good-hearted physician follower. He had no need for it at all, but he took it only to help his follower regain his spiritual clarity and physical activity. He was the ideal example of self-sacrifice and all the deeds were of a humanitarian nature, with the purpose of helping his brothers in humanity to experience happiness in their lives.

Truly, the level of his sacrifice knew no bounds and here we shall tell of another incident.

Once, our noble scholar was suffering a piercing pain that had affected his noble head and caused him to suffer the terrible pain of an intense headache. The physicians were puzzled at his suffering and could not reach a diagnosis to explain the cause of it. However, having discussed the problem at great length some of them came to the conclusion that the cause of the pain lay in his teeth and advised him to have all of his teeth extracted as a solution to his problem. But the scholar understood perfectly well the source of his painful headache, so when they gave him their advice he replied, ‘It is my nerves and not my teeth which cause me this pain. For my teeth are all in good condition and there is no damage in them.’ Nevertheless, he accepted their advice, subjected himself to general odontectomy and had all of his teeth removed. And exactly as he had told them, every one of the teeth was healthy, with no sign whatsoever of dental bacteria or decay.

We ask God to grant him the reward he is worthy of, for the great sacrifices and deeds he rendered on behalf of humanity.

chapters.title: Charity Brings its Own Reward
chapters.html:
Al’lah the Almighty, through His Benevolence towards humanity grants mankind benefits and then ascribes those benefits to them so that the inner self of every man will be displayed and thereby establish which of them is best in deed.

In fact, the Almighty legislated about alms-giving and spending in the fields of benevolence. He imposed it on mankind through the obligation of almsgiving and decreed that it should be an act of charity thereby helping humanity draw nearer to Al’lah, the Almighty. Both of them aim at the purification of the human spirit through the spirit’s approach towards its Almighty Creator in this world and to gain Paradises for this benevolent deed in the Hereafter.

Since all money belongs to Al’lah, He apportioned a share of it to the pauper within the money of the affluent so that the latter may disburse some of it as appropriate and gain goodness through this deed and charity, and draw near to his Provider. And so is it with the pauper who will praise God and get closer to Him by thanking the Almighty Who has granted him this favour. Through that, he will love the wealthy donor who, in turn, will also love the poor for being a means through which he approaches Al’lah, the Almighty.

By such sympathy and reaching out both of them achieve benefits here and in the Hereafter; society, overall, becomes virtuous and happy, and mankind will have greater sympathy and care for one another.

And yet, the true believer has a sense of honour for he will never ask for such benefits, and even without his begging Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) recognises him and discerns his need. The Almighty says, “You know them by their unfailing mark: they do not beg importunately from all and sundry.” ﴿15﴾

Similarly, the one who follows Al’lah’s Envoy will know them well through his link with him (cpth), so he allots an income from the Islamic treasury for them as did the Orthodox Caliphs.

Once the disciple, Abdul-Kadir Yahya al-Dayrani, was out with his eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and while they were strolling the scholar was uttering sublime words which brought to mind the Supreme Attributes of Al’lah the Sacrosanct. As he spoke his face shone with light and brilliance, and his words might be compared to a fountain of precious jewels addressing the perceptions which lead to the indisputable reality in his spirit.

As they walked along the street leading to the Parliament a man sat on the ground in front of it; he appeared to be desperately poor, and hid his miserable face under a large round hat, similar to the caps of the Armenians. Seemingly his neediness, penury, and his embarrassment at the lack of work and income obliged him to hold a small glass box in which he had put some cheap candies and sweet bars aiming to earn his daily bread by selling them, since his self-esteem would not permit him to beg from others and ask them for alms. People were passing by but they failed to see him for they were wrapped in their own thoughts and intent on their own life gains, and they paid no attention to him. It had not come to their minds that he had been overcome by difficulty and dire need, which drove him to sit there: perhaps their behaviour was normal and instinctive since they did not possess the light whereby they could realise the truth… so, they failed to recognise the man in his need.

This man was desperately poor!

Oh my God! Where are those who see by Al’lah’s Light and witness the truth with their hearts? In fact, whether people inadvertently failed to see him or simply ignored him, is all the same, since they were not willing to give him even a few coins or relieve him of his embarrassment; that is why they shunned his goods and failed to buy any of the candies he offered for sale. Even so, he would never ask for alms, but he sat in silence without begging or asking for anything, except inwardly from his Provider.

By God, this is a deserving person on whom a gift would never be wasted, but on the contrary it would secure Paradises for its giver. So, who was the one who, through his insight, recognised and understood him? Surely, he was the only humane person among all those who sought their own worldly benefit: those whose eyes see but whose hearts are blind!

After walking a little ahead of the beggar the merciful master stood and called out, ‘Abdul-Kadir, my son!’

‘Yes, sir…?’ in a questioning tone.

The scholar said, ‘Oh, Abdul-Kadir, do you have a quarter of a lira?’ ﴿16﴾

With no hesitation the disciple said, ‘Yes, sir! I do.’

‘Well… hurry back and give it to that poor man.’

Being mindful of his desire to apply his supreme purpose, Abdul-Kadir went immediately towards the destitute man and put the coin in his hand. Then he returned to his beloved guide. As soon as he arrived, the scholar addressed him again, saying, ‘Abdul-Kadir! Do you have another quarter of a lira, my son?’

‘Yes sir, I do.’

‘Go then, and give it to him, Abdul-Kadir.’

‘I hear you, sir, and will do so!’

He promptly went back to the poor man and laid another coin in his hand, then he rejoined his dear guide who cheerfully said, ‘Abdul-Kadir! Have you seen how great is the reward you have gained for this act of charity?’

Commenting later on the request of our dear guide, the eminent scholar, the disciple Abdul-Kadir, said, ‘In fact I did not realise what I had gained and achieved at that time, as my own insight had not yet been opened, but, my willing obedience for all the orders of that grand master relied on his great sublime insight about which I was certain.

‘My son, Abdul-Kadir! Do you have another quarter of a lira?’

‘Yes sir, I do.’ ‘Go then, and give it to him.’

He handed the man the third coin and so Professor Abdul-Kadir felt that the pauper was overjoyed as he was temporarily relieved of his misfortune. And how would it not be so since he had known that his Provider would respond to him by sending the one who was distinguished by His Light, and knew about his need, and so he helped him. The Almighty says to His beloved Envoy (cpth), “You know them by their unfailing mark: they do not beg importunately from all and sundry.” ﴿17﴾

Only you, Prophet, and those who see by Al’lah’s Light are able to recognise such impoverished men.

chapters.title: A Loveable Human Being
chapters.html:
His heart was overflowing with the greatest love for all of God’s creation in general and for mankind in particular. Whoever sat with him and listened to his words sensed the pure love he carried in his heart for every one of them. Such was the character of the venerable scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. It was because Al’lah loves everyone that he loved them too.

And so, if those who gathered with this noble master were good-hearted and inclined to recognise what is right and true, they would surely love his personality and yearn to meet him because they would feel something of the scholar’s mercy for his associates and his longing for them to receive guidance.

Mohammad al-Shaibani al-Taghlibi (may God have mercy upon him) was an example of such people who loved the humane scholar and had a heartfelt attachment to him at the deepest level. At that time, he was living with his family in the same neighbourhood as the scholar. Mohammad al- Taghlibi had served as an officer in the Faisali ﴿18﴾

Syrian army; he was from Damascus and was a kind-hearted and good natured man.

When the French army entered Syria in the year 1920 under the leadership of General Gouraud after the battle of Maysalun, the French governor gave orders that the Syrian army should be disbanded and its officers assigned as police officers after successfully completing a training course in Amber, the Royal Ottoman Faculty.

Mohammad al-Taghlibi joined this course and outdid all the other officers when he achieved the highest grade of them all. He then joined the same security corps in which our esteemed man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, served as a police officer.

Al-Taghlibi had taken the revered master Emin Sheikho as his ideal and a role model for himself. He was able to understand an aspect of the secret of this pure human being as he witnessed some of his amazing deeds and successful actions in the field. Therefore he had great reverence for him and surrendered to him wholeheartedly just as the noble companions had done with the great Envoy of God (cpth). He was a faithful companion of the scholar and devoted himself entirely to his service.

Then, when the venerable master, Mohammad Amin, established his religious circle after the death of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro (may God have mercy upon him), al-Taghlibi became a loving, faithful disciple of the scholar. He stayed close to him constantly and never once missed the lectures of the scholar where he used to drink from the fountain of his knowledge and sip from his sublime state of being. The time that the two men spent together was not restricted to the periods of the scholar’s teaching, and in fact the venerable master frequently visited his friend and disciple in his home and sat with him in his orchard.

Master Ahmad al-Taghlibi, a son of Mohammad al- Taghlibi, was still a child when he asked his father one day, ‘Daddy… Daddy… who is older, you or our master Amin Bey?’ ﴿19﴾

It seemed as if the question deeply affected the father who answered his son with a look of consternation on his face, ‘Oh son, Amin Bey is more advanced, ﴿20﴾

not only than me, but more than everybody else. You should know, my son, that our master, Amin Bey, was born with the wisdom of a grown man.’ Then he explained to his child what he meant by these words. He related to him many incidents from the childhood ﴿21﴾

of the great scholar during which he, unlike any other child, acted as an enlightened adult. This was most evident after the death of his father when he was left alone at a tender age with his mother, as his elder brother Saleem had travelled away to pursue his studies.

‘At that time, my son,’ Mohammad al-Taghlibi continued his explanation to the young Ahmad, ‘our master, Amin Bey, was only seven years old. He was accustomed to receiving a considerable amount of pocket money from his father. However, after the death of his father he felt that the family’s former level of financial ease had changed considerably and therefore he told his mother that he no longer needed pocket money. From that time on he did not take even the smallest amount of money from his mother. And when she asked him what he would like to eat each day, he chose the cheapest kind of food in order not to burden her with increased household expenditure. As for meat, it was expensive, so he gave it up altogether until he became a young man and began to work and receive wages.’

It is clear that Mohammad al-Taghlibi had great reverence and love for his grand guide and therefore he kept company with him throughout his life. Out of his love for Mohammad Amin and his awareness of the benefits one would derive when listening to his Godly guidance, Mohammad al- Taghlibi’s great wish was that all people should attend the lessons of this great mentor or, at least, have a chance of sitting with him and listening to his words.

For this reason, when the venerable guide came to visit him at his farm, al-Taghlibi soon set about inviting all the workers on his land to come to sit in his presence and listen to some of the jewels and pearls of his revered teaching and wisdom. During one of these visits, Mohammad Amin was sitting on the ground when a large number of the workers gathered around him in response to the invitation of Mohammad al-Taghlibi who had called them to put aside everything they were doing and to come quickly! ‘It’s our master, the great guide,’ he said, ‘he’s come here to bless us.’

Truly, everybody loved this great teacher and guiding light and yearned to listen to his wise, healing words. Therefore the workers soon hurried to see him and so did a nephew of Mohammad al-Taghlibi and other relatives who had a farm next to his.

They all sat around the revered master with hearts filled with joy. Then one of the workers asked the great guide, ‘Oh sir, we all know that Lucifer, the first devil, was created from fire, but I wonder, how will the Almighty punish him with it? I mean, since he is a fiery creature, how will the fire affect him and burn him and cause him to suffer?’

Mohammad Amin always chose his words wisely when addressing people. He would talk to everybody according to that person’s ability to understand, and always quoted an example that would flow straight to his heart and make an impression on it. So, when the man finished asking his question, the venerable master picked up a clod ﴿22﴾

of earth and pelted him with it.

‘Oh… oh…’ the worker cried in pain.

‘What? Did it hurt you?’ the great scholar asked him.

‘Yes sir, it did.’

Then the wise scholar said to him, ‘So… it is the same for you as it is for the Devil. You were created from clods of earth such as this; however, when I pelted you with one of them, it caused you pain, didn’t it?’

At this, the worker nodded his head in agreement, ‘That’s right, sir. Now I understand.’

Such was the wonderful approach that the venerable master used when he answered questions. He knew well how to use his innate wisdom so therefore his answers were convincing and comforting.

Let us turn back to the son of Mohammad al-Taghlibi whose father had guided him to love the venerable master just as much as he himself loved him.

The young Ahmad used to be with the two friends during most of the time they spent together, whether taking a walk or sitting in quiet companionship. The venerable scholar always treated the little boy with extreme kindness and sympathy. He never upset the boy at all, and always allowed him to accompany them whenever he wanted to do so.

Therefore Ahmad was often seen in the home of the esteemed scholar and close to him from the age of five until he became a youth, when the noble scholar departed this world to live in the Presence of his Lord. Thus, because of his father’s love for the great scholar, because of the education which he received at his hands, and due to the mercy and tenderness he sensed in his heart, Ahmad was deeply attached to the venerable master, Mohammad Amin.

On a particular bitterly cold winter’s day it happened that the scholar was at home speaking to some guests with his usual words of great illumination and guidance. Then when he finished and the guests stood up to say goodbye to their host, the imposing master accompanied them to the street door demonstrating his customary kindness and hospitality as it was the first time they had visited him. As he stood at the door, the compassionate master felt the cold air penetrate to the very core of his noble body and before long it was clear that he was suffering from a common cold.

When young Ahmad entered the room of the great guide he saw the symptoms of illness on the face of this man who was so beloved of him and his father. Without delay, and unnoticed by anyone present, the little boy rushed out of the house and ran towards the clinic ﴿23﴾

of Dr. Qarcozian, a famous physician at that time. Ahmad rushed into the clinic and accosted the physician saying, ‘Oh doctor… please come with me. It is our master, Amin Bey… he’s ill. Will you please come with me right now and treat him?’

The physician also had a great love for the august master. He had sensed the kind and merciful manner he had when dealing with people and, at the same time, he was aware of his sound, superior logic. So he immediately answered the little boy’s request and put on his outdoor clothes, while his son quickly prepared the medical bag. Then the physician, accompanied by the little boy Ahmad, hurried towards Mohammad Amin’s house in order to examine him.

When they reached there and entered the house, the physician was surprised to see the greatly revered master enjoying good health. He realised that the renowned scholar had simply caught a chill and there was nothing else to fear or cause concern. Mohammad Amin received the physician warmly and invited him to come in. They entered the sitting room and then the noble master began to speak with his customary gentle, sweet, and enlightening words which were full of logic and conviction, while the physician became fully absorbed in listening to the scholar’s words and understanding their meaning. He was elated to be in the presence of this noble master.

Whenever the physician met him he felt himself flying to the seventh heaven as long as he remained in his presence. He yearned constantly for such meetings where illumination and wholehearted rapture prevailed, and true wisdom and knowledge poured forth from the mouth of the noble guide.

The physician never concealed his belief in the humane master, in fact he expressed it at every opportunity saying, ‘If all of the Muslim sheikhs and scholars had been like the venerable master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, I would have declared publicly that I am a Muslim.’

chapters.title: Attempted Assassination
chapters.html:
It is true that the dreadful event we are about to relate really did take place. This heinous crime was perpetrated one evening against the honest, compassionate scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, though his heart held nothing but pure love for all of God’s creation without exception, and even for those who were his enemies.

But, thank God, the attempt failed! For who could possibly succeed in harming any man who faithfully worships God, and only God?

For forty years, the noble officer, Mohammad Amin, worked ceaselessly to establish the truth and overcome deception. He never failed to lend a helping hand to any needy or oppressed person, to spread peace and justice among the people by arresting criminals, seeking faithfully to root out all crime and wrongdoing, and efface every misdemeanour in the county where he was responsible for security as a police officer. This is how he spent the years of his youth: striving constantly in God’s Name as every single human being should do. Therefore it was no wonder that his Provider chose him and sent His Illumination down to this man’s pure and immaculate heart, thereby revealing to him extensive realms of Godly Knowledge as a reward for his many sacrifices and miraculous deeds.

During this latter stage of his life he adopted a different path; rather than tracking down criminals in his quest to bring about the truth on earth, he set about guiding people in the way to believe in God and become illuminated by His Light, thus leading them to the Godly Presence through his own wise words and his elevated state. The Almighty revealed to him heavenly sciences and granted him great heart life; in turn the scholar delivered this gift to all those who followed his guidance, wishing only to help them enjoy happiness in this life and the life to come.

A great number of young disciples had been drawn to the humane scholar and attended his weekly lessons which he gave in his own house, so that they too might drink from this cup of transcendent knowledge and become aware of the Godly Wisdom behind His Actions.

During these lessons, the noble guide would relate a lofty interpretation of the verses of the Holy Qur’an, explaining God’s high Purposes from His Legislations and the sublime significance of His great Words. His teaching, therefore, was excellent in its expression, perfect in the interpretations it gave, and convincing in its reality and reasoning.

What is more, it flowed gently to the hearts of the listeners, bringing them spiritual life, filled with immeasurable joy and sacrosanct bliss. This is no wonder, for the Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.”

And the fruits of these blessed meetings were that the hearts of those present were refined and enriched with noble qualities such as mercy, tenderness kindness, generosity, justice, bravery, benefaction, wisdom and many others.

This was the course of the venerable guide’s life until, with the passing of the years, he was sixty years old and one evening he was faced, most unexpectedly, with a shocking incident.

During the winter the great guide began his lectures after the sunset prayer and they were concluded by performing the evening prayer at ten o’clock. On that day, as usual, before starting the lesson, the august teacher stood up to perform the communication with God, and all the disciples present stood with him, their submissive hearts fully directed towards the Grand God in the company of their guide. One of the disciples called for the prayer and another, introduced by the venerable guide, stood as an imam to lead the congregation. The lines were perfectly arranged and by uttering the statement ‘Al’lah is Greater’ they began the prayer.

However, within moments of beginning the prayer there was a knock at the door. According to the instructions previously given by the august teacher, if such a thing should occur, the last disciple to arrive at the prayer session would open the door for the new arrival and then return to continue his prayers.

And that was exactly what happened. But unfortunately, the last disciple to arrive that evening, was a new member who had only recently joined the circle of our guide and unfortunately did not yet know all his brothers in the group.

So, when he opened the door he saw a stranger but did not give it much thought because he assumed that the new arrival was one of the disciples whom he had not yet met. He allowed the newcomer to come in and then closed the door and hurried back to his prayers, leaving the stranger to follow him.

But all was not right!

The newcomer advanced slowly towards the congregation until he came to a halt right behind the great scholar. And there he sat on a chair, seemingly waiting in silence for the end of the prayer.…

Such behaviour would have appeared quite normal if anybody had given it any thought, for they would think that he had already performed his prayer at home, and surely someone who had performed the prayer would not perform it again.

The new arrival sat calmly, gazing at the great master who was praying: standing, then bowing and then preparing to prostrate himself on the floor.

Everything continued as normal until the moment when all those present, including the noble guide, prostrated themselves, when suddenly, the stranger leapt from his seat, unsheathing a dagger as he did so, and swooped down towards the virtuous guide. With great force he tried to stab him in the back, seemingly determined to make it pierce his noble heart!

But what a miracle!

Before the criminal’s treacherous hand could hit its target, the scholar flipped over to face his attacker and in a trice, with a sudden powerful movement, he grasped the hand holding the dagger, and then exerted such pressure that he might have broken it.

This skilful art of self defence was one of many outstanding disciplines that the eminent guide had acquired and practised during his service as an officer in the security forces when he struggled with the toughest criminals and lawbreakers.

And so, the precarious situation had been reversed in an instant: the treacherous brute was now lying on his back at the mercy of Mohammad Amin, who had pinned him to the ground, his knee on the assailant’s chest as he calmly picked up the dagger and held it to the man’s throat .

The criminal was taken completely by surprise at the instant reversal in his position; for he could never have imagined such an outcome. He had come to the meeting to kill a man and make a quick escape; but there he was, on his back, petrified and facing death! How had this happened? Neither he nor any of those present could possibly know!

In a trice the assailant had become the victim and was now crying and begging for his life, ‘Oh sir… for God’s Sake forgive me… I beg you sir, forgive me… please…’

His entire body was racked with fear as he believed himself face to face with his own impending death.

The noise caused by the awful struggle had disrupted the disciples’ prayers and they all turned towards the source of the sound where they saw a rather strange and dramatic sight. A young man, crying and begging forgiveness, was pinned to the ground by their awesome guide, his knee placed firmly on the man’s chest, as he held a long, sharp dagger to the interloper’s neck. It was truly an astonishing sight to behold!

How had all this happened seemingly in the blink of an eye? Until the moment when they were all prostrate in prayer there had been no sign of anything untoward for the entire incident had occurred within mere seconds!

On looking carefully at the face of the young man they soon realised that he was a stranger to their group and was, in fact, the latecomer to their prayer session, which only served to confirm his premeditated decision to kill their beloved guide.

Oh… what treachery!

Their hearts suddenly overcome with rage they rushed towards the assailant, intent on tearing him to pieces. But before they managed to reach him the voice of their noble master, Mohammad Amin, boomed out, ‘Leave him to me!’

They stopped in their tracks, in obedience to the command, with all of them endeavouring to suppress their anger. They stood aside, motionless, watching their revered master, with every last man wondering what was to become of the criminal and what punishment he would certainly receive.

As for our just and merciful man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, he pondered the matter and said, ‘I wonder… I don’t recognise him… there is no previous problem between him and me. I clearly remember all the criminals that I caught in the act and punished in the past, when I was a security officer. He isn’t one of them, and he isn’t one of those I used to chase to prevent them committing crimes… so, as far as I know, he has no reason to want to kill me or even bear a grudge against me!

‘So, why did he attack me? I can see that he must have been motivated and misled by somebody else who must be an enemy of religion and truth.’

To be sure of his conclusion, the pious master asked the criminal, ‘You… tell me… what made you do this?’ In a quivering voice, the man told the master his story which was exactly as Mohammad Amin expected.

This criminal was in thrall to another man who falsely pretended to be a religious guide.

That loathsome, fraudulent teacher had used the criminal to carry out his appalling plan and enticed him by offering a large sum of money; worse still, he promised to protect him from any judgement that might made against him if he carried out the crime of killing the noble guide Mohammad Amin. Then to facilitate the task, he gave him a detailed description of the place where the guide was accustomed to meet with his disciples and the exact time that they would start the sunset prayer; thus he had formulated what he thought of as the perfect for this terrible crime to be committed.

Having heard the details of the conspiracy, the tolerant guide lifted the dagger from the neck of the would-be assassin and said to him in a commanding tone, ‘Stand up and get out!’ The man could not believe his ears; but he scrambled to his feet as quickly as he could and ran away, unable to believe that he would really escape what had seemed to be his inevitable death.

Yes indeed. This was how the merciful, pure-hearted guide turned evil back towards its perpetrators! Mohammad Amin allowed his assailant to leave peacefully even though he was fully capable of killing him with the very dagger the criminal had tried to use to stab him through the heart!

However, if the noble guide had killed the interloper he would not have been punished, for neither Godly Law nor human law would have condemned him as his act would have been considered a case of self-defence. He could even have given the felon a sound beating at the very least, and then taken him to the police station where he would have received his due penalty. But even this our merciful guide did not do! Not only did he forgive the man and set him free, and not only did he prevent his zealous followers from causing him any harm, but he also turned towards them declaring his intention, ‘Brothers, I do not want you to mention the name of this man nor of the one behind his actions to anyone at all: for Al’lah is the Coverer of faults and I have forgiven them… both of them. So, I do not want you to go against them or do harm to either of them. Understood?’

Some of the disciples could not hide their astonishment at the unusual reaction of their guide, and they replied in amazement, ‘But, sir, how do you pardon a person that willfully tried to kill you? And furthermore you want us not to discuss this incident with others!’

The venerable master answered them, saying, ‘Listen my sons, I know the person who pushed this cowardly criminal to kill me, but I also remember that his father once did a favour for me and I always return a favour. So, for his father’s sake I have forgiven him and overlooked his sin, and I want you, too, to forget about it and not stand in their way. Okay?’

Truly, there are no words to express the wonderful picture of Godly Perfection that coloured the heart of this merciful human being; a picture that makes us bow our heads, and confess the sublimity and nobleness of its owner.

This story also takes us back 1400 years to the time when the people of Mecca plotted against the truth brought to them by the noble Envoy Mohammad (cpth) and made many attempts to kill him. Nevertheless, when the Envoy (cpth) returned to them at the head of a powerful army after his migration to al-Medina and they fell at his powerful, merciful hands, he stood before them and addressed them in a voice that calmed their hearts and planted renewed life in their spirits, ‘People of Quraysh, how shall I deal with you in your belief?’ They replied, ‘You are a noble brother and a son of a noble brother!’

There and then, the man (cpth) who was sent as a mercy for all the worlds said to them, ‘You may go… you are free!’

By such wise and merciful conduct, the Envoy of God (cpth) captivated his people’s hearts, which led them all to true belief and to follow the mission of truth.

chapters.title: Inspiration or Evaluation?
chapters.html:
Faith, in reality, is the sure knowledge and certainty attained and realised by the believing human spirit itself; thus it becomes a fact settled within the spirit, where the two intermix so that they become as one.

Faith is a moral truth, sensible and tangible to the faithful spirit itself. When a spirit comes towards faith, faith will flow within it just as the light generated by electricity flows through wires, and water flows through the branches of a tree, bringing life to its leaves and flowers so as to help it bear fruits.

Faith penetrates the spirit just like the life force penetrates the body, and then it will be manifested through noble merits, exemplary behaviour and good deeds through which a believer seeks only to see the noble Face of the Grand God and gain His Satisfaction. Neither lowly desires nor personal benefits will be the reason or purpose for such a believer when practising his deeds; he will completely abstain from all that is forbidden and naturally embrace sublime compassionate intentions towards all his brothers and sisters in humanity.

Faith rises in the spirit when recognising the Source of every moment of bliss, light and delight, and the Origin of existence, movement and life. But one will not attain such true faith unless one possesses the firm will to do so; this is the will that stems from the fear of inevitable death. Once the human spirit fears its destination after death it will truthfully seek an escape, and thus will give thought to that which will drive it towards the Creator through the contemplation of His Creation.

Faith is based on the realisation of God’s Existence and the witnessing of His Light with the heart’s eye. When a spirit attains faith it will feel gratitude and give praise to the Benefactor for His countless Graces: this is a feeling completely free from any trace of malice, ingratitude or denial of the truth that may stain one’s behaviour, and behind which one may seek to gratify his own lowly desires.

Through faith, humanity will retrieve their previous connection with God after a foolish separation from Him (Glory to Him), and thus they will return to the Home of their origin after a long trance-like period filled with terrible visions.

They will return to the true glory and honour, to happiness and sublime love, to the heavenly ways of ascension, and to their fascination with the most beloved One Who is above all men and all things. Through faith, mankind will be able to live a life of theopathy after a long period of loneliness; and besides this, they will enjoy lawful pleasures and become enhanced with every desirable and wonderful attribute of perfection.

They will move out from the darkness towards the Godly Light which flows throughout the whole of existence, and thus view worlds of realities and attain observational knowledge that make them relish the Gardens of eternity while still in this mortal world, and before moving on to the Afterworld.

The realms and ranks of high ascent and illumination that the believer enters and ascends are not to be compared with all that the sources of physical light in this life produce or the exquisite beauty that roses and other flowers display. Life, indeed, should be lived as the believers live it, for only the believers perceive the grave purpose behind this life and the precious opportunity it offers humanity to attain high ranks of sublimity and felicity.

As for those who have not yet recognised their Provider and His Supreme Attributes, those who are distracted by their own base desires, infatuated by whatever is transitory and does not belong to them, their life is senseless and fruitless; worse still, it is filled with misery and distress. They have forgotten that sooner or later they will be presented with a long-term prison sentence through the one indisputable fact: death will certainly come to all. They have not thought of their situation after death when they will suffer the terrible flames of grief and sorrow, and much weeping and groaning. Such a destination is the consequence of their own foolish choices and their preference for worldly desires rather than the rewards of the Afterworld; then the only relief available to them on the Day of Resurrection will be the blazing Fire.

They will throw themselves into this Fire even though they are fully aware of the intense pain it will cause them; nevertheless, they will seek it out so that it may help them forget their unbearable spiritual fire, the fire of shame and regret which burns them from inside.

A miserable substitute relief indeed!

Al’lah, the Almighty, provides you, oh Mankind, with food and drink and all that is necessary to sustain life. This provision is for your body, but along with all these material blessings He also provided you with sublime guidance to help you return to Him and enjoy a happy life. If you consider His boundless Favour upon you, you will surrender to Him and gain all that you wish and more, but if you have an elevated sense of self pride you will lose everything.

This universe is like an open book for all people; everybody can read the signs that indicate the Presence and Existence of God, the Almighty, and those signs that show His Supreme Attributes.

If mankind has the inward motivation to study this book willingly, seeking to be guided to the Almighty God, and contemplates the words it contains until he feels love for Him, belief will flow to his heart and grow ever greater as he advances along this path and supports it wholeheartedly against his sick whims and rendering of good deeds.

This is the type of belief that the grand scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, invited people to adopt and emphasized that they should attain. Since the years of his youth he shone with vitality and vigour, unwavering in doing favours and sparing no effort in offering a helping hand to the needy, sacrificing everything, whether cheap or precious, in the Cause of Al’lah. He did not waste a moment by day or by night, and in fact, he was used to spending most of the night hours struggling against criminals and criminality, seeking to curb the corruption and destruction they planted within people’s hearts and in their countries.

Nevertheless, despite all his remarkable feats he never felt for a single day that he was achieving great work, rather he saw all his deeds as insignificant and unpretentious, and only the simple means which would help him to draw closer to God. Had he once allowed himself to admire one of his own deeds he would have lost the accumulated rewards of all his deeds, but this never happened.

Because of his unparalleled truthfulness and excellent capacity, the Almighty Al’lah burnished him and prepared him to ascend to a high grade after He tested him and let him pass through sessions of training in the high Mohammadan school until he graduated as a teacher for all humanity, supported with divine illuminating knowledge.

This took place after he performed a true communication with God in the company of the master of the Envoys, Mohammad (cpth), during which he received a great revelation from God: a donation that qualified him to become a guide to lead people to the Supreme Being. However, he always declared to his followers and reminded them, ‘You will not derive benefit from me, that is to say, from the Godly Sciences which God sent into my heart and then on my tongue unless you truthfully and earnestly follow the path leading to belief in Him.’

Because of his mercy for all creation and his intense desire to lead humanity to God, the Almighty chose this noble man and assigned him to the position of guidance due to the perfection his spirit derived from God that made him surpass all other guides.

When the great scholar witnessed worlds of Beauty and Grandeur of God and acquired high transcendental knowledge about Him (Glory to Him), he looked around and found his brothers in humanity immersed in poor, inferior trappings, away from the essence and realities. No wisdom behind the Godly Edicts was known to them nor were they aware of the way leading to belief.

Others, scientists and researchers, had become immersed in studying the world of molecules and atoms and were wholly infatuated by them, to the extent that they devoted themselves entirely to discovering their laws. They were totally preoccupied by their research, completely forgetting the Grand Creator and Wise Maker, and withdrawing far from the Omnipotent Director and Provider. They did not consider the end towards which they were descending and that one day they would leave everything behind and depart from this world. They occupied themselves with their creature comforts instead of the Creator Who perfectly and singularly created the earth and the heavens. Had they turned themselves to Him and resorted to Him, He would have endowed them with sciences and knowledge incomparable to any of the human sciences.

The eminent scholar always repeated that belief is the only way which allows humans to obtain God’s Favour and unprecedented Rewards. For no human is able to observe the Commands of God and advance in this life within His Bounds, no human is able to follow the Law which leads eventually to happiness in both this world and the world to come and enjoy the Godly Gifts unless they think about the way which makes them truly believe in God and witness His Presence (Glory to Him). The Holy Qur’an stated that miracles avail a human of nothing in this respect if they have no motivation for recognising the Creator of this universe and then moving from the stage of mental belief to the stage of realisation and certainty of God’s Existence that a spirit perceives inside itself; and this is achieved only by following the path of heart belief that was followed by our master Abraham (pth).

Time and again the noble master, Mohammad Amin, emphasised, ‘The Almighty Al’lah created the heavens and the earth, the oceans, and all other beings for one sole purpose: to help man believe that there is no god except Al’lah.’

The revelation and facts presented to mankind by this humane scholar indeed worked as miracles for all people who became aware of them, and indeed no other scholar of religion could present the like of them.

The Almighty corroborated him with the wide knowledge of realities so as to help him in guiding His servants towards the straight path, bringing them back to the right direction and teaching of the Envoy of God (cpth) after they had lost the way of happiness and shunned their Provider.

Beside the lofty revelations with which God provided the noble guide, He also caused him to be the instigator of many extraordinary incidents so as to manifest his high rank with God and his true guidance.

As an example of these incidents, here are two stories that took place with the scholar before some of his disciples.

In the town of Duma in the east of the Damascus region, there was a fertile oasis, provided with fresh spring water called Ain al-Sukhnah. This spot is rich with water and fish and distinguished by its pleasant, gentle breeze.

On one outing, the venerable guide, accompanied by a few of his followers, visited this natural spring where tranquility prevailed and a refreshing breeze was gently blowing. The birds delighted the ears with their sweet song and the ripple of the glistening, abundant water created a wonderful feeling of joy in the spirit.

When the group reached their destination, the venerable guide stepped towards the edge of the spring and stood there looking towards the water with eyes that shone with brightness and vivacity.

Life seemed to gush forth from him like the abundant waters from the sparkling spring, quenching the thirst of the hearts of everyone that joined him seeking to recognise God and wanting to know how to attain His Satisfaction.

The disciples stood around their teacher, some on his right and others on his left, and observed every movement of their master as he bared his arm and stretched his hand into the water in order to scoop up water to drink. But how strange! It is commonly known that fish usually swim away as soon as they sense a strange body entering the water. They either swim away from the spot or take to their hideout, for like all creatures of the sea, they are considered wild animals and their existence differs from the life of all other creatures. It is impossible for them to become tame in the presence of mankind, rather their natural disposition is to avoid people whenever possible.

This phenomenon is known to everybody. But what happened with the noble master on that day bewildered all those who were around him and left them amazed. For the moment that our guide put his hand into the water, they saw great numbers of fish coming in shoals from every direction vying to touch the hand of this honest guide and then they went away pleased and enraptured even if they had achieved only one kiss! This phenomenon brought to mind the sight of the pilgrims when flocking to touch the Black Stone, or kiss it from a distance, ﴿24﴾

and then continuing their circumambulation of al-Ka’ba as though they had had their greatest hope fulfilled.

But what the fish had done with the noble guide did not come from traditions, in fact their behaviour was motivated by their own desire and love, for it is known that animals can receive inspiration. This was exactly what the unusual behaviour of the fish showed! All the disciples who were there stood astounded, unable to believe what they saw with their own eyes. Their astonishment grew even more when the noble master drew his hand from the water and then some of their brothers turned up their sleeves and put their hands into the water to emulate him; however, every last fish turned and swam away to avoid the hands! To confirm what they had seen the first time, the brothers in religion asked their beloved guide to put his hand into the water once again, and at their insistence the noble master complied. Again, multitudes of fish swam from every direction to have the honour of touching the hand of this pure man!

They caressed the merciful hand and then swam away for others to take their place. But who knows! Perhaps there were some fish which were not satisfied with just one touch and so they kept contact with the blessed hand as long as it remained in the water! How odd! Why did this happen with him, in particular? Why not with anyone else?

The great teacher drew his hand from the water and then sat close to the spring while his disciples gathered in a circle around him. Then he began to speak to them about belief and the necessity of man’s attaining a true connection with God. He explained to them that if a human wants to be safe from affliction in this world and avoid disgrace and torment in the world to come, they should not rely on merely performing the formal appearances of worship, rather they should seek to attain true heart belief associated with entering into God’s Presence and witnessing His Supreme Attributes. Only then will they enjoy the bliss and honour that God has prepared for them.

He continued his calm, even-toned speech which bestowed heart life into the hearts of those who were listening to him, and through which he mentioned some stories clarifying the way of true belief. He asserted to them that a human would not reach this level of belief except by repentance, honesty, thought and persistence in his pursuit to attain belief.

This kind of belief is not obtained by accepting it from other previous authorities or traditional sciences, but it depends on one’s own process of thought and daily contemplation of the signs of the universe, all of which are produced and made by the Grand God, until one realises the true Godly Existence and has this fact settled firmly in one’s mind.

A human being should ponder on the creation around them and before this, on their own creation; how they started as a sperm in their father’s loins, and then turned into an embryo in their mother’s womb; how they were born as an infant child and then grew day by day until they attained full maturity.

After this field of contemplation, this thinking person can move to wider fields that help them know more about their Creator. They may think of heaven and what it contains, the day and night, the four seasons, the earth and all that it includes of seas, rivers, mountains… and other great signs. While a person is deeply contemplating and earnestly seeking to know the truth, their spirit, abreast with their thought, directly reaps the fruit of their efforts and becomes fully interested in knowing the reality of this existence, yearning to recognise the Creator and Provider to Whom its destination and return will be.

This is what this grand guide addressed himself to; so, it is likely that God showed this event with him to his followers so that they might truthfully and seriously think about his wise and true teaching which would eventually lead them to achieve happiness in this life and in the life to come.

And here is another odd incident that also took place with the noble master and not with any other of his brothers in religion.

He enjoyed walking, which was possibly due to the nature of his previous work when he was a police officer and he used to walk through flat, grassy land and dry, sandy desert, mountains and valleys, covering large distances on foot. And so, later on, when he retired he adopted the habit of walking daily for many kilometres; he usually did this throughout the year except during the cold months of winter. The great guide appeared to spread light like the shining full moon surrounded with its gorgeous nimbus when he walked with his group from the al-Muhajireen area where he lived towards the mountain of Qasiyun.

They used to go there to escape the noise and bustle of the city where they would breathe the soft, fresh air and enjoy clement weather. They used to sit in a circle around their master at the top of the mountain with spirits having been cleared by the clarity and serenity of their teacher’s noble spirit.

Overwhelmed with a sublime Godly dignity and splendour that came to them through their guide, and with their hearts wholly focused on their teacher, they would listen to his high interpretation of the noble Qur’anic verses which captivated their minds and helped them derive great benefits from the oceans of Benefaction and Donation of the Merciful, Great God. From time to time he would narrate to them stories of great lessons and other examples so as to imbue them with the love of bravery, fortitude, magnanimity, devotion, and noble human sacrifices.

After this heavenly journey, they would start on the return journey having quenched the thirst of their hearts by the outpouring of bliss and revelation that came to them from Al’lah, the One Who knows all that is unseen. He reveals whatever He chooses of this to true believers by virtue of their company with this noble master.

This was no wonder, for the great guide was always with his Provider; so, by such lofty direction and his inspired instruction he could direct the spirits of his followers to his beloved God, and thus enable them to drink from his own great love and passion for his high Lord.

With the end of such a blessed session, all the disciples would have forgotten their earthly existence in order that their spirits should soar upwards to high, heavenly oceans whence they returned with their spirits coloured with the seeds of God’s Supreme Attributes and immersed in bliss, the like of which all the combined pleasures of this world failed to offer.

This explains to us why our great Prophet (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.” On the way back home, and not far from their path, it happened that one of the stray dogs, which had fled from man’s harm and preferred to wander in the mountains, used to follow the guide and his disciples after lying near the place where they sat. Every one of the disciples noticed how the dog ran close to them all during their way back; and whenever their noble guide stopped to speak to them with his affable, pleasant words which delighted the ear, the dog would also stop with them and would then continue to follow them as they went on their way.

Whenever one of them approached the district where he lived or his own house, he would leave the group after taking his leave of his guide; the dog, however, would not follow him.

Instead, it would continue to chase around the procession which, as light as the gentle breezes, would continue on its way through al-Muhajireen where their master lived.

And so, the chasing continued until the merciful guide headed alone towards his home, followed by this dog. Then when he opened the door of his house he would see that the dog had stopped about ten metres away, looking at him intently. So, in a kind and merciful way, the venerable guide would stretch out his hand as a gesture, saying to the dog, ‘Welcome… come in.’

There and then, the dog would bow its head, shake it right and left and wag its tail, and then as quick as lightning it would run away and back up the mountain until it was out of sight. This behaviour with the dog was always repeated whenever the venerable guide took his disciples for an outing up the mountain.

And even though we are subjected to oblivion by nature we shall never forget the deeply moving statement of this great human guide when he sorrowfully commented on this event saying,

‘Alas! The dogs could recognise our dignity but humanity could not!’

These true events are but two of the many that the Almighty effected through this humane guide in the company of various groups of his disciples, so as to turn their attention to his high rank. For, in reality, he was like a shining beacon for them, without which they would have proceeded through this life in absolute darkness.

Indeed, he was like a flower surrounded with beauty and a moon encircled with glory.

chapters.title: The Honest Man
chapters.html:
Fifty years ago, simplicity was a general characteristic of our forefathers, and the era was distinguished by its good, kind-hearted people. Rain fell abundantly over all the lands of Greater Syria, causing the earth to generously produce its blessings and bear fruit. Until that time the unpolluted air was still clean and refreshing, and carried with it the pleasant scents of roses and jasmine which grew in abundance. The prolific trees offered up their abundant fruits and helped to spread fine weather all over Damascus, the aromatic city. The abundant waters of the rivers coursed throughout the land to offer a welcome sight for the eye and to bring joy to the heart: A truly idyllic scenario!

As for the mothers of those times, they were accustomed to staying at home, dedicating themselves to taking care of their children and educating them in the many aspects of an upright way of life. They did not leave the house unless it was necessary to do so, and they were content to be in their homes where they were concerned only with the happiness and well-being of their families. Their houses were usually large Arabian-style buildings, at the heart of which was a spacious sunny courtyard surrounded by beds of fragrant greenery, exquisite, softly hued roses and other charming colourful flowers, which all grew abundantly. And in the centre of every courtyard there would be found a fountain overflowing with sparkling, pure water that breathed life into both the spirit and the soul.

While the interiors of the houses were spacious and comfortable, the roads outside were narrow, earthen lanes, along which hawkers would frequently pass, some carrying their wares and others drawing them on carts, and all calling out what they had for sale.
