One day, beneath the gentle drops of light rainfall, a poor hawker sat on the ground, in the middle of a lane, shedding copious heart-rending tears that stirred the feelings of all who saw him. All around him, there were broken pieces of glassware scattered here and there.

A crowd of people had gathered around the distressed man, trying to comfort him in his misfortune. Some of them said, ‘Don’t be sad, brother, Al’lah is Generous.’ And others said, ‘Take it easy, man. There’s no reason for all this crying. Al’lah will not leave you without provision.’ One of the passers-by added, attempting to console the distraught hawker, ‘Thank God, the evil has been destroyed.’

As for the desolate man, with every consolatory statement that reached his ears, he either shed more tears or snapped back reprovingly, ‘What! What are you saying? You don’t know how great my problem is. I’ve lost all of my goods and I’m now heavily in debt… I borrowed money to buy most of this merchandise.’

And he shouted out, ‘Leave me alone, please, go away… go away!’

The poor peddler was accustomed to roaming the old quarter in Damascus, carrying on his head a large glass box containing many glass plates, cups and other such things.

On that particular rainy day, as he was walking through the muddy street, calling out his wares, trying to earn money to provide his daily needs, he suddenly lost his footing on the soaked, slippery earth, causing him to lose his balance and fall flat on the ground along with all the heavy weight he was carrying on his head. And so, in one unexpected moment the glassware was smashed and he had lost all of his wares.

As the glassware had dropped to the ground, he felt his heart drop into his boots, and with this he slumped to the mud, gazing at the broken pieces with tears in his eyes, and overcome by the awful shock. He remained silent for a while in an attempt to cover the bitter feelings and distress that overwhelmed his spirit, but he could no longer bear it. He burst into tears and began to wring his hands with grief and then slap his cheeks whilst all the time crying and groaning.

At this pathetic sight, people began to gather around the miserable man and to express their sympathy for him; but because of his deep distress, the peddler said to them, ‘Please… please leave me alone… by God, a few years ago, I lost three hundred golden Ottoman liras and I didn’t feel annoyed or even care about it. But today, by God, I feel my heart burning with grief and pain for every broken glass that costs only one golden lira.’

These words reached the ears of the benevolent master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, who was passing along the same road, accompanied by one of his intimate friends and faithful disciples, and the friend’s little son. When the virtuous master heard the statement about the loss of the three hundred golden Ottoman liras he stopped in his tracks, approached the poor man and said to him, ‘Stand up, my brother… come on, stand up and come with me.’

The poor, distressed man wiped his eyes and looked upward to see where these kind words had come from. He found before him a handsome, dignified and honourable man with a bright, radiant face, looking at him tenderly and urging him to go with him.

So, he did as he was asked and stood up. The revered master took the glass seller’s hand and led him away from the crowd, as he whispered in his ear, ‘Come with me, brother, for I have something to say to you.’

Thereupon, the loving friend who was accompanying the noble master approached his teacher and asked politely, ‘May I take my leave, sir? Or perhaps I can come with you, if you do not mind.’

‘With pleasure… come with us. Let’s go together.’

The three men walked away, followed by the little boy, and the crowd was left behind to wonder what the outcome would be. They watched until Mohammad Amin, his friend, his friend’s son and the distressed hawker disappeared into the distance, and then they all lost interest and eventually went off to pursue their own affairs.

The august master took the man home with him. When they reached there he knocked at the door as a caution for the women inside that strangers were about to enter, and that they should go to their own quarters. Then he opened the door and called out, ‘I have some guests with me; make way for us,’ and waited a few minutes before inviting his guests to enter.

They went in to the reception room and sat down. Then the honourable master looked at the miserable peddler and said, ‘Now, I want you to tell me the story of the three hundred Ottoman golden liras which you lost. Would you please tell me how this happened? Where and when?’

The poor hawker sighed deeply before beginning his story, ‘Ah, sir… ah! This happened almost three years ago. I don’t know how I lost them. I was walking along the street holding them tightly in my hand when suddenly they were no longer there.’

‘But, at that time…’ the august man asked, ‘Didn’t you look for them and ask the shops around about them?’

‘No sir, on that particular day I did not give much thought to the golden coins for at that time I had inherited many thousands of Ottoman golden liras, and so the three hundred liras was a negligible sum for me. But, alas, I wasted all of that inheritance for the sake of gratifying my base desires, and eventually I became penniless and all those who had pretended to be my faithful friends then deserted me, and refused to have anything to do with me. Ah, sir, in fact, I paid dearly for my frivolity. I underwent hard and bitter times and experienced all sorts of hardship. I am full of remorse for what I have done! I was immersed in debauchery. I failed to repent for my irresponsible conduct until I was reduced to poverty.’

On hearing this, the august master rose from his seat and left the room for a little while, then when he came back he had his hand in his pocket. He stood before the peddler and asked, ‘Can you give me a description of the purse that contained your three hundred golden liras?’

‘Yes… yes sir, of course I can, for I still remember it very well. I had put them into a small red bag and tied it with brown cord.’

There and then, the virtuous master pulled his hand from his pocket to disclose a bag which was exactly as the hawker had described.

‘Is this your bag of money?’

Taken by surprise, the poor man opened his mouth and stared at the noble master’s hand, and then he stammered, ‘Oh, sir, yes… yes… yes, it is my bag! By God, it’s the same bag into which I had put my money.’

His happiness was beyond description. He was like a withered plant that had been revived by pure water and restored once again to life and vigour.

In the gentlest way, the venerable master dropped the bag of money into the hands of its owner, the miserable peddler, who received it, but still with a look of disbelief written across his face: could this be true? Or merely a dream? His money had been returned to him after a lapse of three full years! Here it was, three hundred golden liras, the exact amount he had lost! God sent them back to him after he had lost hope, all hope of their return and was in desperate straits besides. And so, with this, the joy of life returned to him. With eyes full of tears, he began to praise and give thanks to God for what He had graciously arranged for him.

With the accident that occurred on that day, God (Glory to Him) took from the hawker only a small sum of money but then He compensated him with a great amount. He replaced his dire straits with affluence and his gloominess with well-being. The loss he suffered when the glassware was broken brought him an abundance of good, and his misfortune turned into a great benefit for him.

But how could our honest and faithful man, Mohammad Amin, keep the gold safe and untouched all during that period of time? How noble were his morals! How hightoned was his character that ensured that he abstained from using that gold to obtain for himself the pleasures of this world! For three years, he kept in trust the great fortune he had found and did not spend even one lira of it for any purpose whatsoever!

When he had first found the gold coins, he informed all the shopkeepers in the quarter and also left a written notification at every shop, stating, ‘I have found a sum of money; so, if anyone inquires about it, tell him to visit me and give me a full description of it and then I would gladly hand it over to him.’

But nobody was able to describe the bag and its contents correctly so he hid the bag, with the valuable gold coins in a safe place in his room until God willed that they should be returned to their rightful owner, through this wise, Godlydecreed accident.

From this we learn that although we may suffer grave misfortune, eventually it may turn to our benefit. And this was what happened with the peddler who is the subject of our story.

As we have learnt, the relatively minor loss of his glassware ultimately produced a great blessing for him; and on the other hand, the attributes of virtue and honesty of our humane master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, were openly displayed. For the entire three years that this supremely honest man had the bag in his possession he did not open it except just once when he counted the coins in order to verify their owner. He kept them in trust, waiting for the day when the owner would rightfully come to redeem his trust.

In the Qur’an the Almighty says, “We offered the Trust to the heavens, earth and mountains and they refused to bear it for they feared it; Man bore it. Man was unjust to himself and ignorant of its results!” ﴿25﴾

In fact, the great, eminent guide Mohammad Amin recounted this story to the disciples in his large circle many times, in order to give them an example of the good Guidance of God, the Almighty. He clarified how God, in His Mercy, had deprived the hawker of a portion of his money when he was living a life of frivolity and carelessness and entrusted it to an honest man to keep on behalf of the hawker ﴿26﴾

until the time came when he turned back to follow the path of virtue and justice. At that time, the Almighty decided to return money to the peddler after the gold had increased in value so that he might praise Him wholeheartedly and believe in His Wise Disposal and Merciful Handling with His creation.

chapters.title: Words from the Heart
chapters.html:
Officer Mohammad Amin first met Sheikh Emin when he was in his youth, and thereafter was never apart from him until the day he left this earth.

‘Take this thousand-bead rosary, my son.’ Sheikh Amin Kuftaro, the rector of the Naqshbandi school (may God have mercy upon him) said to his new disciple, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. ‘If you want to join our religious brotherhood, you have to glorify God over each of its beads, one by one, until you finish; and then repeat this five times. This must be done in one sitting.’

This was the way of belief which mankind should follow in the view of the traditional scholars of religion. If one hopes to be a member of a particular creed, one has to achieve the glorification of God as already mentioned, which in reality is simply the repetition of the Name ‘Al’lah’ while fingering each bead of a rosary: a simple verbal exercise which is not associated with witnessing or realisation!

‘Yes sir, I will do it with pleasure.’ the young officer replied.

He took the rosary and headed straight home. He entered the house and went immediately to his room where he sat on a wooden chair with a tightly woven rush seat. He had brought some stones from outside and placed them in a pile on the floor beside him; each time that he completed a round of the rosary in glorification of God he would move one stone to the other side of the chair. He held the rosary between his fingers and began his veneration of God, ‘Al’lah… Al’lah… Al’lah…’ He murmured this continuously until he completed one cycle of the rosary and bent down to move a stone to the other side; then he eagerly turned back to his absorption in repeating the Name of Al’lah, his most beloved One.

What an amazing act of reverence it was! Truly it was beyond comparison with any similar action carried out by others. It was as though a flame of the greatest esteem and veneration for the Grand God flew from his noble and pure mind to the lofty and supreme Side of God, the Source of all might and power, the Creator of all beauty, and the Lord of all goodness and perfection.

What a wonderful opportunity it was for this pure and virtuous spirit to practise its soaring and sublime love, to turn wholeheartedly to its most beloved One, celebrating and basking in His Supreme Attributes. Indeed, there was not a single atom of his heart that was not fully immersed in boundless love and yearning for His Excellency, the Almighty God.

A considerable time elapsed but the noble master did not move in the slightest from his original position. He was wallowing in his love for the Supreme Being of God, sinking deeper and deeper, with no feeling of boredom or weariness.

How could he feel bored or weary when he was living in a high state of recognition of his most beloved One.

This is how human beings should glorify God. It was the unmatched and irrepproachable love he had for his Lord which made him truly glorify and exalt Him.

Many hours had passed before he focused again on the present moment and paid attention to the rosary and the stones. He remembered the obligation he was fulfilling and so he counted the stones which he had moved unconsciously from one side to the other and found a total of twenty five!

‘Oh… oh… what have I done?’ the venerable master said to himself, ‘How have I moved all of the rosary beads twenty five times? Sheikh Emin told me to glorify God for only five rounds of the rosary!’ He felt as though only a few minutes had passed, although in fact it was many hours. If he had not been conscious of abiding by the words of his sheikh, he would have continued in his glorification of God… but for how long would he have done this?

He had been sitting on the chair for so long without making the tiniest movement, that when he stood up the chair was attached to his clothes. In fact, he had been so absorbed in the glorification of God that his body had become numb. It was as if he had shed his body and left it motionless on the chair and then taken flight with his spirit, his heart filled with longing and passion for his Grand God, as he swam in worlds of sanctity and realms of majesty, beauty and perfection. What great love for the Almighty God was enclosed within his heart! Indeed, it was beyond compare and totally irreproachable.

Once, after undertaking this dignified guidance to Al’lah he expressed his great love for God when addressing his disciples, ‘Oh, sons, a question has struck my mind: in the world of the first creation when we were still abstract spirits before the creation of our physical bodies, I wonder, did I love God before He loved me, or was it He Who loved me first?’

He appeared engrossed in profound thought that denoted his immeasurable faithfulness and boundless passion for God, and then answered the question himself, saying, ‘It is Al’lah Who loved me before I loved Him. The truth is that Al’lah loved all creatures before they loved Him.’

Indeed, through his illustrious and honourable behaviour the venerable scholar set the pattern for the way that all humans should follow to love God, and take as an example for their own success in order to rise to high spiritual levels. Out of his great love for God and his devotion to Him, whenever he engaged in a discussion with inquirers he was careful not to quote Qur’anic verses as proof to confirm his explanations and thoughts which were all inspired by the wisdom of Godly Guidance. Rather, he would use eternal, logical and irrefutable proofs depending on the varying implications of the noble Qur’anic verses, and always refrained from quoting any text from the Holy Qur’an.

This was because he was concerned in case the inquirer did not understand the Godly Purpose and might, therefore, shun Almighty Al’lah within his heart, think badly about Him, or even deny His Words, glory to Him. Therefore, it was customary for Mohammad Amin to offer his explanation, set out his argument and give his proof which were all revealed to him by the Grand God and derived from His Holy Book. If he found that the inquirer was convinced by the answer and showed satisfaction with the reply, he would then quote the noble verses which confirmed his Qur’anic thoughts and explanations. But when his answer was not accepted by the inquirer and the explanation he gave about the Godly Wisdom behind His Words and Acts did not appeal to them because it was not in line with their illusory notions, then the merciful scholar would refrain from mentioning any Qur’anic verse. He preferred to make himself an object of criticism and to be wrongfully accused by the people than to let them utter one untrue word about his beloved Lord and cause their hearts to turn away from their Creator. Truly, he sacrificed himself entirely in order to avoid such reactions.

What arouses one’s amazement is the strange and deep effect and impression that his words had on those who heard them, the like of which had never been observed in any other human being. The chain of words flowed constantly from his heart to theirs, for everything he said was issued forth from a deep well of realities that he had witnessed with his own heart’s eye; therefore these words could touch the hearts of those who listened as they spoke to their inner core, and they would then move towards the actual truth.

As regards those who are taken up with embellishing their manner of speaking, composing elegant style and interspersing the meanings with complex statements, their words will leave no impression on the hearts of those who listen to them nor will they lead them to a greater understanding than they already have. The following account serves to illustrate this.

There was a certain respectable professor who lectured in universities. This professor had attended some lectures given by the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho and admired them greatly. So, he decided to speak with the scholar’s wisdom: he learnt some of the lectures by heart and used his distinguished explanations when addressing people. Indeed, he began to speak about these sciences, using his customary embellished manner of speaking and well-formed statements, and quoted proofs so as to confirm these thoughts. However, despite all his efforts and attempts to mix the philosophy he had studied with the divine sciences he had learnt from the scholar, and despite his eloquent way of addressing people, he failed to leave any impression on the hearts of those who listened to him. He admitted this situation once and declared in amazement, ‘How strange! I speak classical Arabic and use rhetoric in the best way, and I offer appropriate proof and quotes, however, I am unable to convince those who listen to me, or even touch their hearts; whereas the scholar speaks in the simple vernacular, and still he impresses people with his words and captivates their hearts and minds until they become completely convinced of his thoughts!’

This is the simple truth; for guiding people to Al’lah is not accomplished by giving lectures about memorised sciences or repeating knowledge derived from text books, nor by using fluent phrases or elegant style. Spiritual guidance is an invitation to Al’lah depending on the clear insight of the guide. The heart of a real guide should be vibrant and engrossed in the state of witnessing the Presence of Almighty Al’lah and His Supreme Names, and of observing the realities of the noble verses of the Holy Qur’an. Such being the case, the tongue of the true guide will transform the state of his own enlightened heart into words which will flow directly to the hearts of those who listen to him, transmitting the high state in which he lives and will lead them, if they truly seek to recognise the truth, to the same witnessing of the lofty realities to which he is witness.

This is why the personality of this great scholar made a deep and unmatched impression on everyone who listened attentively and yearned to know all that is right and true. His words expressed the Qur’anic realities he had witnessed. Therefore people became entirely absorbed in his noble speech which flooded from the ocean of God’s Peerless Words, and was filled with wonders and marvels. Yet, beside the effect of his words on people’s hearts he also embraced them with his lofty spirit in which the illuminating Manifestation of Al’lah descended upon him and the lights of His Supreme Attributes brightened his spirit. These were the divine realms to which his heart led them, realms by which his own heart was captivated and which he constantly yearned for.

How many times had he incidentally come across hardhearted people, people whom, nevertheless, he had been able to impress through his unparalleled illumination of truth and rectitude. The eminent scholar spoke about one of these meetings with such people that had come about through God’s Will for He arranged this meeting out of His Mercy for these kinds of people.

Once, when the great scholar was in Aleppo, he came across one such person in a public park, so he seized the opportunity and began to talk to him about God, revealing His kind Treatment with people and His great Love for them. Despite spending a long time talking to the man, he noticed that he was not in the least bit touched by his words. His pure heart looked into the man’s heart and found it to be as hard as stone, containing no hunger for his Creator, the Almighty, and totally unaffected by the lofty words he spoke in his endeavour to offer him guidance.

What a strange character! Indeed, the venerable scholar had never met a man with such a callous heart, so unaccepting of the description of God’s Tenderness, Mercy and great Favour upon His creation; in fact, this was a man who showed no appreciation of His deep Wisdom behind His Commands. It seemed as if his heart was impervious and therefore he failed to draw even a hair’s breadth closer to God.

This man reminded the august scholar of the episode with the great Envoy Mohammad (cpth): he (cpth) suffered so much with the people of Mecca whose spirits were as hard as the rocks of Mecca Mountain where they lived. When this thought struck his mind, pure tears filled his eyes and began to pour forth. He remembered the great efforts that the Envoy (cpth) had expended to bring those people out of the darkness and turn them towards the light, and to turn them from their errant ways and in the direction of guidance, until finally their hearts were in the right place. Thus, by mentioning God they, in turn, became messengers and set about enlightening people about God’s Mercy, Tenderness, and other high Supreme Attributes.

That night, the merciful scholar could not sleep. He spent the whole night weeping out of his tenderness for that man who was living totally estranged from God and whose heart was as black as the darkest night.

The next morning, the revered master, showing renewed energy and vitality, went to the same park so as to inhale clean, fresh air. He had to wait there for some legal business to be completed and it was God’s Will that he should again come across the same person he had met the day before. He approached him immediately and sat beside him on a bench where he began to talk to him with gentle words filled with deep significance about Godly Compassion.

Mohammad Amin talked and talked, trying to implant in him even the smallest particle of his immeasurable love for God until, eventually, the man was touched by his words and his heart began to respond and relent. With this, the man cried and cried. Oh… thanks be to God! At last, this callous man tasted the sweetness of being close to God by virtue of the company of the one who was talking to him and instructing him.

At last, his spiritual state changed from one of indifference to one of awareness and he began to mount the ladders of transcendence.

Another incident took place in the year 1963, when the ambassador of Yemen in Beirut visited the august scholar, Mohammad Amin, in a house belonging to one of his disciples in the city.

The Yemeni ambassador was fully engrossed in the scholar’s words and listened attentively to the holy explanation: his heart was totally enthralled and submissive to the point that he became wholly captivated by the character of the noble scholar.

Then, at the end of this meeting, which lasted for three and a half hours, the ambassador asked permission to take his leave having quenched his heart’s desire and enjoyed sweetness and delight such as he had never experienced before. It was the sweet taste of being close to the Almighty Al’lah, the like of which he would not find in any worldly pleasure or entertainment. He sensed that his heart had been nourished, his spirit relaxed, his knowledge and wisdom developed, and even that it had attained a high and sublime quality.

When he left this glorious meeting he bade goodbye to the venerable guide after expressing his gratitude towards him and his hope that he would kindly allow him to visit him once again in the same house.

Since the compassionate scholar had received a favourable and positive response from the Yemeni ambassador and he noticed the advantages he had attained from hearing the truth and the proper guidance, he welcomed the ambassador’s request for a second visit. Because he was so eager and sincere in his request, the ambassador came to meet the great guide the next day and was so happy to be allowed to attend another lecture of his precious lectures.

The venerable master again received the Yemeni ambassador with great warmth and welcomed him with pleasant words. And again, a sublime and divine revelation flew from the noble mouth of the great guide and as on the previous day, this meeting also lasted for three and a half hours, until the Yemeni ambassador felt that he had satisfied his heart and mind by unprecedented, lofty words, the like of which he had never heard before.

He left the great guide while experiencing an intense state of deep and heartfelt affection, mixed with an overwhelming feeling of appreciation for the new devout thoughts that had never come to him in the past.

Let us now return to our beautiful, ancient city of Damascus, and particularly to the house of our great scholar where he sat talking to his family, his wife and daughters, giving them enlightening advice that would be helpful and advantageous for their life to come. As they sat together, the great guide quoted some of the ideas and examples he had brought up in his conversation with the Yemeni ambassador.

When the family heard about his meeting with the ambassador, Mohammad Amin’s wife, wanting to have some idea about Yemenite fashion, asked her husband to describe the ambassador’s clothing to her.

The noble master remained silent for a short time while he tried to recall the ambassador’s apparel, but how strange! He could not remember a single detail of the ambassador’s appearance to relate to his wife! What an odd reaction from the great master! It was evident that he had been totally consumed with his words of guidance. He had sat face to face with the ambassador during two long meetings, each lasting at least three and a half hours, but he had no recollection of the ambassador’s apparel or even of his features! How strange!

Truly, the revered master was concerned only with the heart of a human and not with the outer body and its accoutrements. It was man’s heart which he looked for. He knew well that guidance flows to the hearts of people and takes its place therein, for it is there where the essence and core of humanity exists.

Then, as we shall see, it was God’s Will to release the venerable master from the tight corner he found himself in because of his wife’s request. At that moment, Al’lah directed the scholar’s son-in-law to the house; so when the august master saw his son-in-law coming, he quickly called him, ‘Come here, my son!’

The son-in-law approached his father-in-law saying, ‘Yes sir… I’m here.’

‘Come and describe to your mother-in-law the clothes of the Yemeni ambassador whom we met in Beirut. Help her to picture the style of Yemenite fashion.’

Thereupon, the son-in-law embarked on a formal description of the outer man.

Such was the distinguished character of the great scholar. He did not care one iota for external shapes or appearances. The heart of humanity was his chief concern.

The following is another incident which confirms what we say:

One day, a disciple belonging to the circle of the great scholar accompanied one of his friends to a lecture. He was hoping that his friend might be guided to the straight path when attending and hearing the teaching of his revered master. They sat together listening to the devout words of the venerable scholar, and then when the lecture finished, the two friends were given permission to leave the hall. In the street, the disciple asked his friend, ‘What’s your opinion about the lesson, my friend?’

The friend replied, ‘The Godly chants were wonderful and the lesson was momentous. Indeed, it captivated the hearts and minds of all present. But I wonder, why does the scholar let that Bedouin recite the Qur’an when his voice is not beautiful and there are many followers with melodic voices in his circle?’

Before mentioning the great scholar’s startling reply to such a question, we want to introduce the Bedouin mentioned above to our noble reader.

The man reciting the noble verses of the Qur’an was, in fact, a commanding officer in the Iraqi army. He sacrificed his high dignity and sold his house in Iraq and then came to Syria, leaving behind all his relatives and friends, seeking only to be near to God and acquaint himself with all that is right and true. He lived in the neighbourhood of the great faithful guide. He was truthful in seeking God and he sacrificed all he had that was precious to him in order to be closer to Him, the Great God (Glory to Him). Therefore, the compassionate guide chose him to be one of those who recite the Holy Qur’an in his circle although there were many of his disciples who had dulcet voices, which delighted the ear and captivated the heart, whereas the Iraqi did not.

One of these disciples asked his guide time and again to let him recite the Qur’an instead of the Iraqi man, but every time this request was met with an absolute and decisive refusal.

Now, let us go back once again to our great scholar who, a few days later, learnt of the conversation that took place between the two friends about the recitation of the Holy Qur’an in his chamber. When he was told of the question which the new-comer asked his friend, the humane scholar uttered his famous statement, ‘Look, my son! I do not want sheer sound intoning the Qur’an… no, I want a human being with a sensitive heart to recite it.’

That Iraqi man had a living heart which enjoyed closeness to God by virtue of his company with the humane guide and his reverence to him. Such a human can touch the hearts of people, for when words come from the heart they will reach the heart. The one who has a living, sensitive heart impresses other hearts, while the one who has a beautiful voice will leave an impression only on the ears. They can enrapture people and amuse them but they cannot touch their hearts and lead them to God.

The secret of guidance flows into the heart and therefore it is always the main focus for every true guide. And it was said, ‘It is good to vocalise the verses, but to put them into practise is better.’

chapters.title: Al - Fara Palace
chapters.html:
Al-Fara Palace

What is al-Fara Palace? Surely there is no one living today who had the good fortune to behold the beauty of this magnificent house and its exquisite gardens. In fact, this palace was already of a considerable age by the end of the nineteenth century. So what could its story be?

On the slopes of Mount Qasiyun, close to the mosque of Sheikh Muhyiddin Ibn Arabi, there once stood an Arabianstyle house with a spacious courtyard. It was an awe-inspiring sight with its splendid architecture and classical style and structure. And making it appear even more wonderful and pleasing to the eye, was the Yazeed River, a branch of the Barada River, which flowed through the grounds of the house. This natural wonder gave the courtyards the appearance of an earthly paradise where the fresh, luxuriant foliage drew life from the abundant waters and the exquisite hues of the multitude of plants and espaliers, Damascene roses and other fragrant flowers were interspersed with the artistic architectural pieces created by man.

One day, as the venerable master, the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho was strolling in the company of Sheikh Ali al- Tikriti (may God have mercy upon him), he happened to glance through the open door of a substantial house and noticed the airy spaciousness of its interior and a hint of its unique and splendid beauty.

He promptly turned his eyes back to Sheikh Ali saying, ‘May Al’lah grant happiness to its owners.’ Sheikh Ali heard the words of the esteemed master, but made no comment and they resumed their walk.

Time passed, and some days later, when the honourable master was at home, there came a knock at the door, and on opening it he found a man standing there. The man was holding a bag from which he drew out an envelope containing some official papers. He asked the scholar ‘Oh sir! Is this the house of Mr. Mohammad Amin Sheikho?’

The honourable master replied, ‘Yes, it is, and I’m Abu Fathi (Mohammad Amin Sheikho)… can I help you?’

The man said, ‘Congratulations Bey… on your new house… may it be blessed!’

The man introduced himself as a bailiff from the Damascus land registry, whereupon he took a paper from the envelope and asked the venerable master to sign, asserting that he had received official notification. Then, he said, ‘Allow me to offer my congratulations again! The entire house now belongs to you, master.’

With a look of astonishment clearly etched on his face, the noble master replied, ‘Which house do you mean, brother? I think you have mistaken both the person and the address!’

‘No, no master! Aren’t you Mr. Mohammad Amin Sheikho?’

‘Yes… yes… that’s me.’

‘Is there anyone else who has the same name as you in this quarter?’

‘No, brother, there isn’t.’

‘So, I haven’t made a mistake… you’re the man I’m looking for and this paper issued by the Damascus land registry office affirms that you bought this property, in its entirety, and therefore it all belongs to you personally. So, would you please sign this paper to confirm that you have received these documents?’

Still taken aback, the honourable master said, ‘Oh, brother! I don’t own anything like that nor have I bought this house from anyone; what’s more, I don’t know anything about this house or even where it is located. Evidently, there must be a mistake!’

The bailiff found the words of the honourable master most odd… then he replied, ‘Oh, distinguished sir… my job is restricted… all I’m required to do is to confirm that you are the person in question, hand you this envelope and get your signature to prove that you have received it; so I’m unable to correct any possible mistake. You’d better go to see the manager of the land office and repeat to him what you have just said to me.’

Early the following morning, the honourable master took all the relevant papers and went to the land office where he met the manager and explained the matter to him in detail. Then, he said, ‘Surely there is something wrong and it must be put right as this house has been transferred into my name, even though it has never belonged to me, nor have I bought it recently.’

There and then, the manager called the employee and asked him to bring the necessary records. He opened them at the page detailing the property under discussion and scrutinised it carefully. Then he said, ‘Oh, Bey! There’s no mistake… you bought this house from a man called Ali al- Tikriti!’

As soon as the noble master heard the name of Sheikh Ali al-Tikriti, he understood fully what was causing so much confusion. He then said goodbye to the manager of the land office and went immediately to Sheikh Ali with the title deeds in his hand.

As he was accustomed to do, Sheikh Ali welcomed him wholeheartedly and was extremely happy at the unexpected arrival of his friend. Having exchanged customary greetings, the two men sat down together.

The august master wasted no time in asking, ‘Why did you do that Sheikh Ali?’

Sheikh Ali replied, ‘Oh, sir! It’s merely a simple present. I hope it is befitting to your elevated rank… I believe that it is suitable for you, sir, and would like you to accept it from me! Please do so!’ Sheikh Ali pressed the honourable master and urged him to accept this house, until finally he even swore by God that Mohammad Amin had no option but to do so.

At this point, the noble master interrupted him saying, ‘I’ll accept it, Sheikh, but only if you allow me to reimburse you. That’s my one condition for accepting it.’

Eventually, through the persistence of the honourable master, Sheikh Ali yielded saying ‘As you wish master. I’m at your command!’

‘What does this house cost then?’ asked Mohammad Amin.

Sheikh Ali said, ‘It’s nine thousand, five hundred majeedi, ﴿27﴾

sir.’

‘But, Sheikh Ali, such a house would not be sold for less than eleven thousand, five hundred majeedi!’

Sheikh Ali said, ‘Oh please, sir! I had already decided to sell this house for the price I mentioned. It is something that I said to my spirit; I never lie to my spirit and always keep my word. So, I’m telling you that this is the price I had decided on and I will not change my mind.’

The honourable master refused to settle for that and the discussion continued back and forth until finally the notable men of the quarter were brought in as mediators to resolve the case. Eventually, their binding decision was to divide the difference between the two sums equally, and so it was agreed unanimously that they should settle on ten thousand, five hundred majeedi as the price for the house.

Once Sheikh Ali had agreed to abide by this decision the venerable master said, ‘Oh Sheikh Ali! I don’t have the whole amount now, therefore, I’ll pay you half now and the rest will be paid in instalments… by Al’lah’s Will.’ Sheikh Ali replied, ‘That’s fine… as you like, sir!’

As time passed, Sheikh Ali received one payment directly after another, until he had received the entire amount and then he came to the noble master and said, ‘Oh master! I’ve received the full price of the house, in fact, even more, so you’ve fulfilled your responsibility towards me.’

This house remained the property of the honourable master until, from the kindness of his heart, he saw fit to give it to the blind and disabled people amongst whom he specified a caretaker and allocated to him a monthly salary from his own money. At that time, people were still accustomed to offering goods and charity, so, they used to bring food, drink and clothes for those who were disabled and far less fortunate than themselves.

This gratifying situation remained like this until the Ministry of Religious Endowments grabbed the house and claimed it as its own. Later on, and under dubious circumstances, the property reverted to the ownership of one man (a contractor) who ejected all the blind and handicapped residents who had made the house their home. He wanted to construct a modern building in its place (a block of foreign-style flats) aiming to sell them at a very high price and earn a fortune.

In accordance with his plans, he demolished the house and began to drill the ground to lay the foundations. But he was in for a surprise! During the excavation work, the engineers in charge of the project were surprised to find a copious spring of fresh water which burst forth where they were digging to lay foundations. It was extremely difficult to control or dam the spring because of its natural abundance, and they eventually managed to do so but only after employing various experts and technicians who supervised the blocking of the spring. This proved to be a ruinously expensive exercise.

The costs were so great that they surpassed the combined costs of the building works and the price of the house itself.

Moreover, before the completion of the building, the contractor died suddenly, without any prior warning, and departed this life to go to his Provider to account for this terrible, wrongful deed.

chapters.title: Sublime Instruction
chapters.html:
As the human body might need a medical doctor to cure physical ailments, the man we shall tell of here was truly a spiritual doctor, a teacher and a guide who refined and healed the heart. Without doubt, this is absolutely the highest rank and greatest mission in this earthly existence, and is strictly entrusted by Almighty Al’lah only to him who is deserving of it. To him He will then unveil the spiritual conditions of those around him who resort to him, those who are under his care and wing, and those whom he educates. Al’lah revealed to him by His Godly Light the slightest thing which may be on a person’s mind… on my life! This is the noble rank of guiding, the mission of the honourable Envoys and Prophets and those who adopted their guidelines, until they too reached that greatest level.

As was his custom, Scholar Mohammad Amin had gone to visit his dear friend, Mohammad al-Taghlibi in his orchard which contained various types of fruit trees, but most of which were apricot. The venerable master would come to this orchard and sit in the shade of its trees inhaling the fresh air, and neighbours and visitors would gather around him to hear his illustrious sermons and lessons, and the sublime wisdom issuing from his noble mouth. This orchard was close to another, similar one which belonged to Mr. Taghlibi’s sister.

That day, the imposing master, Mohammad Amin, arrived with his son-in-law, Abdul-Hadi and two other disciples. He sat under a big walnut tree, enjoying the welcome shade cast by its branches, and closed his eyes to rest, while the other visitors wandered around the orchard with Mr. Taghlibi, enjoying the pure, invigorating fresh air.

There was also a young boy, eight years old, Ahmad, the son of Mohammad al-Taghlibi; the child was also enjoying the fresh, fragrant air and ran off to the end of his father’s orchard where he found some ripe apricots which had fallen on the boundary between his father’s orchard and that of his aunt. The child was accustomed to seeing his father bring to his sister all the fruits that had fallen between the two orchards: he did this because of his serious devotion even though he knew that the apricots always fell on the boundary line of both orchards yet he never kept any for himself..

But on that day, while Ahmad was running and playing he passed close to his aunt’s orchard where he noticed two fallen apricots. He wanted to keep them for himself, so he put them into his pocket, and continued running here and there, while the seeds of doubt began to grow in his mind as he thought of his father’s usual habit. ‘My father usually collects all the apricots here for my aunt, but I have taken those two apricots… and they might have fallen from my aunt’s trees!’

So, even at that tender age, young Ahmad felt as if he had committed a sin and his spirit began to have doubts about his own behaviour.

Meanwhile, he approached the noble master and stopped a short distance from him, and even before Mohammad Amin opened his eyes, the child heard the venerable guide addressing him, ‘Ahmad, my son! Go at once and return the two apricots to where you found them!’

The honourable master’s words came as a great surprise to young Ahmad and he thought, ‘How odd! When I took the two apricots, I was hundreds of metres away from my dear lord… he couldn’t see me and I couldn’t see him so, how could he know what I had done and that I felt so uneasy that I had a twinge of conscience?’

Quite taken aback, Ahmad stood as though rooted to the spot, many questions revolving in his thoughts… and he replied, ‘Yes sir, I’ll take them back immediately.’

Indeed, and in spite of the closeness or possible agreements between his father and his aunt, Ahmad understood that the concern and doubt which had preoccupied him might cast a permanent shadow of guilt over him, whereby he would never forgive himself. That is why the honourable master ordered him to take them back, for by doing so he would receive more purity, piety (illumination by God’s Light), and awe of God’s Goodness.

And to this day, Ahmad still wonders, ‘How could the scholar know what was going through my mind, and what was hidden in my pocket?’ And he says to himself, ‘Surely, it was through Al’lah, the Prescient, as he was deservedly a guiding teacher and doctor to whom the Almighty Al’lah reveals all that may help him in performing his supreme function and sublime mission.’

This is a perfect example of real heart medication, the refining insight, the loftiest humanity and unparalleled education.

chapters.title: The Revelation of the August Master about Performing Ablution
chapters.html:
In his seminars of guidance, Mohammad Amin Sheikho used to show us the wisdom behind each one of Al’lah’s Orders in His Wise Book, the Holy Qur’an: so he clarified and explained the purpose behind performing the ritual ablution and the great wisdom behind this Godly religious duty. He did this in a simple way unprecedented by any scientist before.

And now, Godly Wisdom has appeared showing that the practice of ablution was enjoined by Al’lah in order to incite activity within the body, whereas all Muslim sheikhs have said previously that it is simply for physical cleanliness.

Ablution is performed so that the body’s vitality will energise the human being and open his spiritual awareness. Consequently, the spirit will understand the meanings of the noble verses which are recited in the communication with God, and form a real link with Al’lah; thus the spirit will be purified and gain virtue and every Perfection from the Almighty. After achieving this, all the deeds of those who pray will become good, beneficent and worthy, since every spirit will be filled with it: for any vessel can only give up what it contains.

Now, due to the explanation of this truly eminent guide the wisdom and truth in its great logic have been revealed, as has its utmost necessity. So, inner vitality is the purpose behind performing ablution, that is, to arouse activity within the body just as the sensitive, mindful spirit of the human flows through its nerves which will reflect on the spirit’s heightened power of perception, and will open the feelings of sensibility, and ability to understand and comprehend God’s Speech: thus, the link with the Almighty Al’lah will be realised. This has been clarified by the august master who spoke about it, elucidating facts previously unstated by all other Muslim scientists who agreed unanimously on the opinion that performing ablution had been imposed for mere external bodily cleanliness.

Indeed, bodily cleanliness can be achieved by washing, though it is good to become clean through ritual ablution, yet this is not its main purpose. How could it possibly be for the simple purpose of cleansing the outer body?

For example, suppose a person, who just waking up from sleep, hears someone speaking, would he understand the words immediately or might he understand the spoken words after some moments, just as he would if he first washes his face, hands, feet, and wipes his head to his neck and ears where all these parts of the skin are considered as zones of sensory terminal points? Of course the difference is so vast between the two levels of comprehension and perception.

And here is another example: suppose that person has performed the ablution and got up after sleeping for just an hour, would he need to cleanse himself again even though he is already clean and has not been subjected to the slightest pollution whilst asleep for that short time?

Now, suppose that he got up to pray and worship God at night; might he fall asleep while prostrating himself and remain there asleep if he had not performed the ablution? While, on the other hand, if he performs the ablution he will become revitalised and have his senses opened and become more alert, and hence, he will communicate in a state of full wakefulness after a period of sleep.

Professor Abdul-Kadir al-Dayrani, the disciple of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho spoke to us about his venerable scholar, ‘This noble master used to accompany his disciples from Damascus city, walking across the surrounding mountains, heading for the Basseema region. Whilst walking, Mohammad Amin was amusing them with his pleasant instructive words which included interesting stories rich in lessons and science.’

Basseema is a region that lies on the banks of the River Barada, twenty kilometres away from the city. It is an area marked by its natural beauty, pure air and abundant water. It was in that direction that the virtuous master was walking, and his presence was like the luminous sun which penetrates the sky and sends forth its sympathetic, warm and glowing rays in every direction, with his devoted followers clustered around him like glittering moons deriving their light from the halo of their sun.

The procession might take two or three hours to arrive at Basseema, the lush and verdant spot, where shortly after their arrival they would all sit, and within a few minutes they would fall asleep where they sat, tired after the long walk in the heat; that is, all except that merciful master, since as soon as he arrived at Basseema his noble body would dive into the water of the River Barada to be fully immersed in its refreshing waters, even if only for a few moments, with the intention of performing the basics of the ritual ablution; thus he did away with every notion of fatigue and became fully revitalised. Then, he would put on his clothes and open a discussion with the inhabitants of the village, giving them the benefit of his lessons of great guidance and seeming for all the world, like a lion in his movements and sublime dignity. So, neither fatigue nor sleepiness nor inactivity would affect him. On the contrary, he would appear illuminated, full of strength, vitality and energy, with his bright face like the sun, beaming with life and radiance, and with joy and cheerfulness inscribed on his noble cheeks.

So, as we learn, the first aim in performing the ritual ablution is to achieve exceptional vitality. Thus, performing the ablution before prayer removes the weakness and feebleness of humans, and puts an end to the influence of sleep, so that they will be attentive, lively, and more perceptive and discerning of Al’lah’s Order, and by that they will truly gain the advantage of prayer.

Similarly, in the case of bleeding which entails renewal when the body languishes or weakens, and performing the ablution serves to recover bodily activity and receive the prayer in the best state of awareness and perception.

chapters.title: A Timely Vision
chapters.html:
After the venerable master Mohammad Amin Sheikho assumed the mission of guide and mentor, he set about leading and disciplining people, and directing them to love Al’lah whereby they would find happiness and Paradises to rejoice in during their real life, and to be saved from Hell and its burning fire.

Because of Al’lah’s Love for all of His creatures, he, too, had great love for them: he spared neither effort nor sacrifice in striving to save them from the darkness of turning away from Al’lah and guiding them towards the light which would draw them near to His Presence. This was his paramount aim for he was so merciful and gentle, with a heart full of compassion towards the Almighty’s creatures.

One day, our venerable master was passing through a particular street in Damascus on his way home. As he walked along he appeared to be crowned with a halo of magnificence, reverence and majesty. Suddenly, this imposing master turned around for some reason… and at the very moment those who were walking behind him saw his noble face, they felt the earth tremble beneath their feet, they became dizzy and fell down awestruck because of his appearance of extreme reverence. But why did this happen to them? What had they seen in the features of this merciful, honourable master? What a strange and amazing incident!

This incident reminds us of another, similar, one: a poor man came to Al’lah’s Envoy, Mohammad, (cpth) asking for his help to retrieve his money from Abu Jahl ﴿28﴾

who had extorted it from him. No sooner had Al’lah’s Envoy gone to Abu Jahl and asked him to return the money to its poor owner than Abu Jahl gave him the money as he did not dare to oppose or even question him; in fact, he fell into a state of panic at the thought that he might be killed if he refused. When he was asked why he had given the money to our master Mohammad (cpth), he replied, ‘On each of Mohammad’s shoulders I saw a lion that was about to pounce down on me… so, how could I refuse his demand?’

The solemn master, Mohammad Amin left the men in the street and continued walking to his house. He became deeply affected and aroused by the incident of the terrified men. As soon as he arrived at home, he began to weep copiously since he thought himself to be one of the dwellers of the Fire, since he remembered the saying of Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth), “Everyone who terrifies others shall be in the Hellfire.”

He passed the night in a state of utmost grief: he wept and wept till eventually he was overcome by troubled sleep during which he saw a vision. In this vision he saw Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) talking to him and reassuring him saying, “Give glad tidings to the people of Syria, about thirty two or thirty-four.”

Hence, this august man woke up and understood the meaning of the vision for it was a good omen from Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) at which he felt great happiness and overwhelming bliss. He understood from the words of Al’lah’s Envoy that there would be between thirty-two and thirty-four people in Damascus who would be illuminated by Godly Light and be rescued by virtue of his guidance. In turn, they would become guides for the people of Syria, and then for the whole of mankind.

chapters.title: Every Hardship Is Followed by Tranquillity
chapters.html:
The title of this story is a noble verse which states a firm Godly Law. It is a true account of a situation that concerned our wonderful scholar and guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and reveals the validity of this Law.

A new building had been constructed in the district where the great scholar lived. It was a building in the French style, several stories high, and much taller than the surrounding Arabian-style houses, but it still lacked some finishing touches to become fit for habitation. It must be said that buildings of that type were still rare at that time when the vast, airy Arabic-type houses still prevailed.

The house ﴿29﴾

of our truthful guide was built in the traditional style around a large central courtyard. Its many simple, but pleasant rooms evoked a relaxing and joyful atmosphere; as the fresh air flowed freely throughout the entire house and the gentle rays of the sun brightened every corner. The courtyard was a haven of peace with its many plants and beds of fragrant flowers; but this idyllic setting was soon to be disrupted.

In previous stories, we have mentioned that the noble scholar, Mohammad Amin, had dedicated his house to teaching people the rules and realities of God’s Religion. His disciples used to meet regularly one evening a week with the lesson beginning after the sunset prayer and ending with the reciting of the evening prayer. Apart from the weekly gathering, there were daily meetings which the noble guide arranged to welcome any new visitor who came seeking knowledge about the Godly Statute or an answer to an obscure question.

In this way, the religious meetings continued, with no disturbance to disrupt the lessons or the benefits resulting from them. But a day came when the august guide sat alone in the courtyard of his home, his impressive body exposed to the rays of the sun, enjoying its gentle light and benefitting from its enveloping warmth. He gazed towards the new construction which towered above the walls of his house and noticed that the framework of the building was finished and there remained only the plastering of some of the walls to complete the work.

Looking beyond, into the immediate future, the noble guide began to contemplate the altered atmosphere which would be imposed upon his religious lessons. The new building, which had considerably more floors than any of the surrounding houses, was divided into individual apartments, meaning that there would probably be a great number of residents. But the principle problem for Mohammad Amin was that .one wall of the new structure, in fact, the wall facing Mohammad Amin’s house, had a great number of windows which would allow its occupants full view of the courtyard.

Truly, it was a serious problem!

How would he be able to give lessons to his disciples within full view of everyone living there? He felt certain that the new neighbours would stand at the windows watching the teacher and his students, and surely they would talk and pass comment, thus causing a certain amount of noise that would confuse the hearts of his followers and divert their attention.

No doubt the students would not understand the lesson as well as they should, for the purity of their spirits would certainly be affected by the new circumstances.

They would be constantly on the lookout for people watching them and the quietness that had prevailed until now would surely be missed. As a result, the lectures of guidance would stop for they would serve no purpose. But this would be so difficult for the noble guide and his followers; for neither he nor they could dispense with these assemblies of religious teaching which brought spiritual life and beatitude to his heart and theirs and guided them to live in Gardens in this earthly life before the life to come. No wonder, for the Envoy of God (cpth) said in his noble saying, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.” And because of the benefits the followers gained from their leader through these meetings, the Almighty God would reward him with great gardens and benefits.

It would be so hard if they were to be denied these gardens of Paradise!

In fact it would be a disaster, so what was the solution? He could sell the house and buy another one, but this would take a long time during which the lessons would stop and the benefits accrued from the abundant blessings would also stop. The believers would therefore remain at that level of belief, an outcome which neither God nor His saint, the scholar, wished for them.

These thoughts, and his conception of the coming days, caused the merciful guide to become quite distressed and morose out of his fear and love for his disciples. He could not bear to think about the enormity of the probable outcome, but he could think of no viable solution.

He had spent many years in polishing the spirits and habits of his followers and instilling elevated ideas in their minds and perfection in their hearts. Would all his efforts come to nothing? Would he lose everything? Would his lessons come to an abrupt end and, with that, the disciples’ progress in the way of belief halted?

A sudden knock at the outer door of the scholar’s house interrupted his train of sorrowful thoughts, so he stood up and went to open the door.

He was most surprised to see one of his old colleagues who had served with him as an officer in the military and the police force. It so happened that they had not seen each other for about twenty years, nor had they been in the habit of visiting one another’s homes all during their previous military association.

So, what drove this former colleague to visit our venerable guide at that time?

And, more to the point, what made him remember the noble master after so many years?

The compassionate guide gave a warm welcome to his old friend and invited him to come in, but despite this surprising visit he could not overcome his own gloominess and grief.

When everyone had taken his seat in the large courtyard, the friendly officer noticed signs of suffering on the face of the noble guide so he asked him,

‘What’s wrong with you, Bey? You are not in the usual joyful mood which I remember as always captivating one’s heart. There must be a serious problem causing you to be so preoccupied, and I hope it isn’t bad news.’

With a heavy heart, our merciful man replied in the same doleful tone,

‘Oh my friend, I don’t know what to say…’

‘Come on, my friend,’ said his colleague, ‘tell me what’s bothering you.’

With his finger pointing at the new, towering building, the noble guide began to relate his problem to his friend, ‘Look at this building!’

‘Yes, I’ve noticed it; what’s wrong with it?’

‘As you see my friend, the west wall of this building faces my house and its many windows will allow its new inhabitants a very clear view into my house. So, whatever screen I might erect to shield my house from the sight of the new neighbours would be useless because of the height of the new building. As you know, my friend, I have dedicated my house to the service of God by giving weekly lessons to my followers and daily lessons to all visitors who come in search of further knowledge about religion, or to ask questions. My house has become a mosque to hold meetings of holy knowledge. But when this building is occupied in the coming days, all these lessons of guidance and divine knowledge will have to stop because of the lack of privacy, and so my disciples will be separated from me and their unity dismantled. This is what is causing me such sorrow and affecting me so deeply.’

Then, the friendly officer said, ‘Is that all that grieves you, Bey? Oh, my friend! It’s a simple matter that can easily be resolved.’

‘A simple matter? This tall building will stop me living in my own home and suspend my role of guiding people… and the law is on its side. It truly is a disaster, so how can you say that it’s a simple matter, dear friend? And how can it easily be solved?’

‘As I’ve told you… and I always keep my word… you can consider your problem to be over. Now, Bey, don’t you want to know why I decided to visit you today? I have brought good news. I have been appointed to the position of a chief commander of the military police in Syria.’

Our compassionate guide replied, ‘Oh congratulations my friend, I’m happy to hear this wonderful news; I offer you my wholehearted congratulations.’

The friend said, ‘Thank you, Bey. And now perhaps you understand why I’m telling you not to worry. For sure, within just two hours your problem will be solved and everything will be as you would wish.’

They drank coffee together then the high-ranking officer shook hands with his friend, the noble guide, and left after promising again to resolve the problem that very day.

At that time, the military police had absolute power and a free hand over all citizens. They had the full support of all the appropriate authorities, to help them overcome those who broke the law.

And without delay, the officer proved to be a man of his word!

Soon after the friendly officer had taken his leave of Mohammad Amin, a large police car, and a second smaller one, drew up outside the towering building and discharged a number of policemen. Without delay, they rushed into the building and soon came out shepherding the workers before them and carrying all the building material that they had found inside. They loaded everything, workers and materials, into the two cars and quickly moved off.

At the same time, another patrol car of the military police headed towards the home of the building contractor, where they lost no time in arresting him and taking him to the prison of the military police.

Inside the prison, the unwitting man, who was upset and confused, as he had no idea why he had been arrested, witnessed various instances of suffering and the severe punishment that criminals received at the hands of the police. He knew he was innocent, but his heart was in his mouth for this was a dreadful sight to behold… a sight that made his entire body tremble with fear.

Later on, he was taken to the office of the chief commander, the friend of our noble guide, who threatened him because of the building which commanded such an intrusive view of the house of the magnanimous guide. The contractor had no other choice but to swear by the Great God and to give his word of honour that he would not allow any window, in fact, not even the smallest hole, to open on the wall overlooking the house of the scholar. He promised to make windows on the other sides of the building which would have no possible view of Mohammad Amin’s house.

At this, the commandant released the man together with all his workers and the equipment that had been seized after he told the contractor that he, personally, would, ensure that the contractor fulfilled his promise.

Still in a state of shock, the contractor lost no time in giving directions to his workers to close all the openings on the side of the building facing the house of the venerable guide. But he did not content himself with this measure; he extended the high wall, which already reached from the ground to the roof, with a second wall of about two and a half metres in height which he built on the roof.

And by taking such steps the contractor did truly fulfill his promise, and the house of the noble guide became completely shielded from the view of the new inhabitants of the multi-storeyed building.

The Almighty said, and His (Glory to Him) Words are always true, “Every hardship is followed with ease.” This noble verse states that when a human holds lofty and sublime intentions, God surely will dispel their worries and change the difficulties they might face into a state of ease. Is there any purpose loftier than that of a human who strives on behalf of his brothers in humanity, seeking only to help them enjoy happiness in this life and the Afterlife?

Will not God (Glory to Him) drive away all his troubles and set his mind at rest?

The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “All of creation is dependent on God, and the most beloved to Al’lah is the one who gives more service to His dependent creation.” This multi-storeyed building is still standing in the al- Muhajireen area in Damascus until today. Whoever happens to pass by will see one of its walls completely void of any window or balcony. Next to it, they will also see the wonderful Arabicstyle house of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, although no other house of this type remains anywhere else in the area.

THE END

Praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds
